derivations.claim: **The bar on a finite cut.** On a finite cut take the reduced finite product of the tensor factors $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ and equip each factor with its own normalized bar of [F3]. The finite-product theorem [F1] produces an involutive semilinear bar on the tensor product, compatible with the factor bars; by [F2] the basis of this module is the set of column monomials $M_A$ of the cut. This defines $\psi$ on each finite cut.

**Triangularity.** In the actual positive-first-factor quasi-$R$ convention, every nonconstant term raises the weight in an earlier tensor prefix and lowers the complementary suffix by the same positive root. The prefix-dominance definition therefore puts every resulting label strictly below $A$. The constant term is one, and each factor bar fixes its ordered minuscule wedge vector. The finite-product divided-power integrality makes every coefficient a Laurent integer, proving the displayed triangular formula.

**Involution and parenthesization independence.** Both properties are inherited from the finite-product theorem [F1]: applying the tensor bar twice returns the original element because each factor bar is involutive and the quasi-$R$ twist is inverted by the inverse factorization; reassociating the tensor factors replaces the product of quasi-$R$ twists by its twisted product, and the intertwining relations [F1] identify the corresponding bars.

**Integral monomial lattice.** Since $\psi M_A$ differs from $M_A$ by integral combinations of lower monomials (step 2.1), the $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$-span of the $M_A$ is stable under $\psi$; the same holds for $\psi^{-1}=\psi$.

**Upper cuts.** Consider a larger upper coordinate interval and a tensor supported on the old alphabet. A positive operator in an earlier prefix can only replace a letter $a+1$ by $a$, never create a letter above the old upper bound. Every quasi-$R$ term involving a new upper-boundary root therefore kills that prefix. Terms supported on old roots agree with their old-cut terms, and the fundamental bars fix the same ordered vectors. Reassociate successive prefixes using step 2.2. Thus the larger bar restricts to the old bar, rather than relying on an incorrect letter-replacement description of the factor bars.

**Common lower tails.** After appending $k-1$ to every factor, each earlier tensor prefix has every wedge occupied at $k-1$. Any positive-root word involving the new boundary must apply $E_{k-1}$ at some stage. Earlier positive replacements on old roots preserve that occupancy; $E_{k-1}$ either encounters no $k$ or attempts to create a duplicate $k-1$, and kills each factor, hence the prefix. The entire quasi-$R$ correction involving the new boundary is zero. The old-root toral weights of the appended tail are zero, so all surviving old-root terms and factor bars agree with the old calculation. This proves $\psi\iota_k=\iota_k\psi$ on finite products. Common-root string operators and integral lattices are preserved; uniqueness of balanced lifts therefore preserves the actual charts and bases. No assertion says all new generators vanish on the image.

**The direct limit.** Every vector of the full Fock module lies in the image of some finite double cut, and every calculation in the expansion of $\psi$ is finite and stabilizes in a cut containing the residue and the input and output supports by steps 3.1, 3.2. Hence the compatible family of bars defines a bar on the direct limit, still involutive and triangular, and it fixes each ordered fundamental wedge. No infinite series is taken.

**Conclusion.** On every finite cut the Fock module has the ordinary compatible bar $\psi$ of (1)-(2); the upper-cut and common-tail embeddings commute with it by (3), so it descends to the full bounded or semi-infinite module. All uses are confined to actual finite-Cartan based fundamental factors; neither a universal two-sided-unbounded tensor-bar theorem nor an arbitrary integral quasi-$R$ action is asserted.

citations.quote:
Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\alpha$ be a root of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra
$\mathfrak g$ with respect to a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, with coroot
$h_\alpha$ as in [[def-coroot-of-a-lie-algebra-root]]. Then there are
$e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ and $f_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ with

$$[e_\alpha,f_\alpha]=h_\alpha,\qquad [h_\alpha,e_\alpha]=2e_\alpha,\qquad [h_\alpha,f_\alpha]=-2f_\alpha .$$

Consequently the span of $e_\alpha,f_\alpha,h_\alpha$ is a copy of
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ inside $\mathfrak g$
([[def-special-linear-lie-algebra-sl-two]]).

Let $\mathfrak h$ be a Cartan subalgebra of a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, and let $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ be the root
spaces of [[def-root-and-root-space-relative-to-a-cartan-subalgebra]] for
$\alpha\in\mathfrak h^*\cup\{0\}$, with $\mathfrak g_\gamma=0$ whenever
$\gamma$ is not a root or $0$. Then
$$[\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_\beta]\subseteq\mathfrak g_{\alpha+\beta}$$
for all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathfrak h^*$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published root-space and $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ suppliers. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a
finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra
$\mathfrak h$, root system $\Phi$
([[thm-the-root-set-is-a-reduced-crystallographic-root-system]],
[[thm-root-space-decomposition-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra]],
[[thm-root-spaces-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra-are-one-dimensional]]),
positive system $\Phi^+$ with base of simple roots
$\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$
([[def-positive-system-and-base-of-simple-roots]],
[[def-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]]), and let $J$ be a
subset of the simple indices $\{1,\dots,r\}$. Write $\Phi_J$ for the root
subsystem spanned by the simple roots indexed by $J$,
$$\Phi_J=\Phi\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\alpha_j:j\in J\},$$
and let $H_j=h_{\alpha_j}\in\mathfrak h$ be the coroot of $\alpha_j$
([[def-coroot-of-a-lie-algebra-root]] via
[[def-killing-dual-vector-of-a-root]]). Put
$$\mathfrak h_J=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{H_j:j\in J\},\qquad \mathfrak z_J=\{h\in\mathfrak h:\alpha_j(h)=0\text{ for all }j\in J\},$$
and define the following subspaces of $\mathfrak g$, where $\mathfrak g_\alpha$
is the root space of $\alpha$
([[thm-root-space-decomposition-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra]]):

$$\mathfrak s_J=\mathfrak h_J\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak l_J=\mathfrak s_J\oplus\mathfrak z_J=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,$$
$$\mathfrak u_J=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Phi^+\smallsetminus\Phi_J^+}\mathfrak g_\beta,\qquad \mathfrak v_J=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Phi^-\smallsetminus\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\beta,\qquad \mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J .$$

Here $\Phi_J^\pm=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^\pm$ and $\Phi^\pm$ are the positive and
negative roots with $\mathfrak n^\pm$, $\mathfrak b$ as in
[[def-positive-and-negative-nilpotent-subalgebras-and-borel-subalgebra]]. The
construction depends only on the positive system and on $J$. The following
structural facts are part of the definition (proofs and references in the
Remarks; $\operatorname{rad}$ and $\operatorname{nilrad}$ are those of
[[def-radical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]] and
[[def-nilradical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]]).

**(1) Decomposition of the Cartan.** $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak h_J\oplus\mathfrak z_J$
and $\dim\mathfrak h_J=|J|$, so $\dim\mathfrak z_J=r-|J|$.

**(2) The semisimple part.** $\mathfrak s_J$ is a Lie subalgebra of
$\mathfrak g$; it is semisimple, and its root system with respect to the
Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h_J$ is $\Phi_J$, with positive system
$\Phi_J^+$ and Weyl group $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle\le W$
([[def-weyl-group-of-a-root-system]],
[[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]).

**(3) The reductive Levi algebra.** $\mathfrak l_J$ is a Lie subalgebra with
root system $\Phi_J$ relative to $\mathfrak h$; it is reductive as in
[[def-simple-semisimple-and-reductive-lie-algebras]], with center
$\mathfrak z_J$ and derived algebra $[\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak l_J]=\mathfrak s_J$;
$\mathfrak h$ is a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak l_J$ and the Weyl group of
$(\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak h)$ is $W_J$. The algebra $\mathfrak l_J$ need not
be semisimple: its center $\mathfrak z_J$ is nonzero as soon as $J\ne\{1,\dots,r\}$.

**(4) Parabolic and radicals.** $\mathfrak l_J$, $\mathfrak u_J$, $\mathfrak v_J$
and $\mathfrak p_J$ are Lie subalgebras
([[prop-brackets-of-root-spaces]]); $\mathfrak u_J$ is an ideal of
$\mathfrak p_J$, $\mathfrak l_J$ stabilizes $\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathfrak v_J$,
and $\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\ltimes\mathfrak u_J$ is a semidirect product
([[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]]). Moreover
$\operatorname{nilrad}(\mathfrak p_J)=\mathfrak u_J$ and
$$\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak p_J)=\mathfrak z_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J .$$
Consequently $[\mathfrak p_J,\mathfrak p_J]=\mathfrak s_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$
and the quotient $\mathfrak p_J/\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak p_J)\cong\mathfrak s_J$
is semisimple: in the sense of
[[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]], $\mathfrak s_J$ is a semisimple
Levi factor of $\mathfrak p_J$ and $\mathfrak l_J$ is the reductive complement
to the nilradical. The parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$ contains $\mathfrak b$ and
$\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\alpha$,
the span of the negative root spaces of $\Phi_J$; for $J=\varnothing$ one has
$\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b$, and for $J=\{1,\dots,r\}$ one has
$\mathfrak l_J=\mathfrak s_J=\mathfrak g$ and
$\mathfrak u_J=\mathfrak v_J=0$.

**(5) The positive grading.** There exists $\zeta\in\mathfrak z_J$ with
$\alpha_j(\zeta)=0$ for $j\in J$ and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ for $i\notin J$. With
respect to $\operatorname{ad}(\zeta)$ every root space $\mathfrak g_\beta$ has
weight $\beta(\zeta)$, so:

* $\mathfrak l_J$ has degree $0$ (all of $\Phi_J$ vanishes on $\zeta$);
* $\mathfrak u_J$ has strictly positive integral degrees
  $\beta(\zeta)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$;
* $\mathfrak v_J$ has strictly negative integral degrees.

In particular $\mathfrak u_J$ is nilpotent by this positive grading, and both
$\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathfrak v_J$ have finite-dimensional fixed-degree
slices of their PBW algebras:
$\dim U(\mathfrak u_J)_d<\infty$ and $\dim U(\mathfrak v_J)_d<\infty$ for
every $d\in\mathbb Z$ ([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published category-$\mathcal O$ theory. Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard
parabolic of
[[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with
reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$, nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$ and Weyl
group $W_J$; the ambient category is $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]
with standard objects the Verma modules [[def-verma-module]].

**(1) Dominance for the Levi.** A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant**
if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all
$\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular
$\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$; see
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]] for the ambient
notion).

**(2) Generalized Verma modules.** For a $\mathfrak p$-dominant $\lambda$ let
$E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained
from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight
$\lambda$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero. Define the **generalized Verma module**

$$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$

**(3) The parabolic category.** The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely
generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which
$U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely, that is, on which every vector lies
in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule; equivalently, every vector
lies in a finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak l_J$-submodule and is annihilated by a power of $\mathfrak u_J$
(local finiteness for the nilpotent $\mathfrak u_J$).

The following structural facts are part of the definition; the arguments are
given in the Remarks.

**(4) Generalized Vermas lie in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.** For each
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$, $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is an
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ with highest weight $\lambda$, and the
natural surjection $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$
exhibits $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ as the largest quotient of the Verma
module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(5) Simples.** The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly
the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral
([[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]).

**(6) Serre property.** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects,
quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$; in particular it is an abelian
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ stable under finite direct sums.

**(7) Costandard objects.** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ put
$\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, the restricted
dual of [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]].
These are the **costandard objects** of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; each is
naturally a submodule of the ordinary dual Verma $D M(\lambda)$. They need not
be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Restricted Chevalley duality is an exact contravariant equivalence $D:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{op}}$, with a natural isomorphism $D^2\cong\operatorname{id}$. It preserves each weight-space dimension, the formal character, and every simple composition multiplicity.

Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in root dominance for every $j<l$: the difference of the two prefix weights
is a nonnegative integral combination of the simple roots $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$. This is the coordinate-prefix criterion verified below, and
is defined for these weight vectors rather than only for partitions
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]); then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For every finite-dimensional representation $\rho:\mathfrak g\to
\mathfrak{gl}(V)$, the trace form is bilinear and symmetric, and it is
invariant in the sense that

$$B_\rho([z,x],y)+B_\rho(x,[z,y])=0.$$

Consequently the Killing form has all three properties.

derivations.claim: **All graded pieces and the crossing trace.** A positive root has degree equal to the number of omitted simple roots in its support. Hence the full positive radical is $\bigoplus_{d>0}\mathfrak g_d$, not generally $\mathfrak g_1$. The simple outside root vectors lie in $\mathfrak g_1$ and their negatives in $\mathfrak g_{-1}$; together with $\mathfrak g_0$ they generate the Lie algebra. For $H\in\mathfrak g_0$, $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{>0}}\operatorname{ad}H=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+\setminus\Phi_{\bar J}^+}\alpha(H)=\gamma(H)$ on the Cartan. Both sides vanish on the derived Levi, so this identity holds on all of $\mathfrak g_0$. In particular $\gamma$ is a Levi character.

**Restricted coinduction and the two actions.** Every component $N_{-r}$ is finite dimensional and $N_0=\mathbb C$. Give $N^{\#}$ its regular transpose bimodule actions $(nf)(a)=f(an)$ and $(fn)(a)=f(na)$. PBW gives $N^{\#}\otimes_N U=N^{\#}\otimes B$, carrying its right $U$-action. On the other hand restrict a $B$-linear map $U\to\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B$ to $N$ using $U=B\otimes N$. A homogeneous map of degree $d$ sends $N_{-r}$ into $B_{d-r}$, hence is zero for $r>d$. Consequently it has finite support in $r$, and the remaining domains are finite dimensional. This proves $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B)=N^{\#}\otimes B$ even though $B_0$ is infinite dimensional. The left action is $(XG)(u)=G(uX)$. Its Lie relations follow from associativity in $U$; restriction to $N$ gives an algebraic action on $S$. The left $N$-action and right $B$-action already commute with the entire opposite action.

For homogeneous $X,Y$ of opposite degrees, take the $P$-block trace of $[\operatorname{ad}X,\operatorname{ad}Y]$. Its terms entirely within $P\mathfrak g$ form a commutator and have trace zero, leaving exactly $\omega(X,Y)$. The bracket has degree zero; its adjoint trace on $\mathfrak g_0$ is zero since that algebra is reductive, so step 1.1 gives $\omega(X,Y)=\gamma([X,Y])$. For degrees whose sum is nonzero the crossing operators have nonzero degree and trace zero, and $\gamma_0([X,Y])=0$; degree-zero pairs have no crossing terms and $\gamma$ annihilates their bracket. This proves the displayed identity for all $X,Y$. For degrees $1,-1$, only $\mathfrak g_0$ crosses the boundary, giving the stated $\mathfrak g_0$ trace. For the root $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ example it is $2$, whereas the full trace on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ is $4$.

**Normal ordering.** Choose a basis $H_i$ of $\mathfrak g_0$. For $X\in\mathfrak g_1$, PBW uniquely defines maps $C_i^X,R_X:N\to N$ by $aX=Xa+\sum_iH_iC_i^X(a)+R_X(a)$. All these maps have degree $1$; higher negative degrees of $a$ are retained. On $f\otimes1$ the left formulas are $H(f\otimes1)=-(f\operatorname{ad}H)\otimes1+f\otimes(H+\gamma(H))$ and $X(f\otimes1)=f\otimes X+\sum_i(fC_i^X)\otimes(H_i+\gamma(H_i))+(fR_X)\otimes1$. For $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ right multiplication gives $(f\otimes1)Y=(fL_Y)\otimes1$, where $L_Y$ is left multiplication on $N$. Comparing the two PBW expansions of $(Ya)X=Y(aX)$, with $[Y,X]=\sum_ic_iH_i$, gives $C_i^XL_Y=L_YC_i^X+c_i\operatorname{id}$ and $R_XL_Y=L_YR_X+\sum_iL_{[Y,H_i]}C_i^X$.

**Restricted endomorphisms and the inverse functor.** Transposing a homogeneous left $N$-endomorphism of $N^{\#}$ gives a homogeneous right $N$-endomorphism of $N$, because its homogeneous pieces are finite dimensional. Such an endomorphism is multiplication by its value at $1$. Transposition reverses composition, and summing finitely many degrees gives $\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})=N^{\mathrm{op}}$. For unrestricted maps this argument produces a product of degrees: in the polynomial example $x$ acts locally nilpotently on the dual basis, so every power series in $x$ acts, and these are all the endomorphisms. Its $\zeta$-locally finite subspace under commutator is exactly the polynomial subalgebra; unrestricted completion is therefore explicitly excluded.

Substitute these two identities into $X((f\otimes1)Y)-(X(f\otimes1))Y$. All terms with a nonconstant operator on $N$ cancel; the remaining scalar is the difference $\gamma([X,Y])-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, multiplied by $f\otimes1$, and is zero by step 2.1. For $H,Y$ the cancellation is $[\operatorname{ad}H,L_Y]=L_{[H,Y]}$. The same relations on $f\otimes b$ follow by induction on a word in the generators $\mathfrak g_0,\mathfrak g_1$ of $B$: commute right multiplication by the next generator past $Y$, whose bracket lies in $\mathfrak g_0$ or $\mathfrak g_{-1}$. Since $U$ is generated by $\mathfrak g_0,\mathfrak g_{\pm1}$, both actions commute everywhere. Thus higher radical degrees require no extra assumption; their relations are already relations in the coinduction and tensor models, and their crossing traces were checked in step 2.1.

**Left PBW, without a dimension shortcut.** The map $U\otimes_N N^{\#}\to S$ is left multiplication on the inclusion $f\mapsto f\otimes1$. Its PBW domain is $B\otimes N^{\#}$. For a homogeneous $f$ filter first by its nonnegative dual degree and then by the ordinary PBW length of the $B$-word. In the formula for $X$, every correction decreases the dual degree; in the formula for $H$, corrections preserve that degree but decrease the $B$-length. Thus the map on the associated successive quotients is precisely the vector-space interchange $b\otimes f\mapsto f\otimes b$. Inducting over the dual degree and, at fixed degree, over PBW length proves surjectivity. A finite linear relation has a largest pair of filtration indices; its leading symbols are independent under the interchange, proving injectivity. Each expression involves finitely many words, so the argument needs neither finite dimension of $B_0$ nor a completed series.

From the right PBW model $T(M)=N^{\#}\otimes_N M$, so free finite rank becomes cofree finite rank. From the left PBW model $H(K)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_N(N^{\#},K)$, which is free finite rank by step 2.3. Tensor-Hom adjunction supplies the unit and counit. On each shifted rank-one summand they are the identity under the endomorphism identification and the evaluation map, respectively, so both are isomorphisms. A short exact sequence of graded free finite-rank objects splits over $N$ since its quotient is graded free. A sequence of graded cofree objects splits over $N$ since its subobject is graded injective: $N^{\#}$ is the graded coinduction of the field, and its Hom functor is the exact dual of the corresponding homogeneous component. Hence $T,H$ preserve the exact sequences at issue.

**Duality and standards.** Restricted duality with the principal antipode gives an exact anti-equivalence from finite cofree to finite free objects; the transpose of that antipode identifies the two regular transpose actions on $N^{\#}$. Finite homogeneous components give biduality, so composing with $T$ gives $\Phi$ with inverse $H\circ(-)^{\#}$; no involutivity of $T$ is assumed. For $M=U\otimes_B E$, tensor cancellation gives $T(M)=S\otimes_B E=N^{\#}\otimes E$. On the augmentation vector $\varepsilon\otimes E$, the Levi action in step 2.2 is the original $E$-action plus $\gamma$, since $\varepsilon\operatorname{ad}H=0$. Dualizing makes the generator space $\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*$. The positive radical annihilates this generator space by degree, and the negative regular action makes the dual free on it. The induced PBW map is therefore an isomorphism $\Phi(M)=U\otimes_B(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*)$. This is a standard for the same parabolic.

A finite standard flag is graded free over $N$ of finite rank, since its standard sections are such and every extension splits over $N$. Applying $\Phi$ gives a reversed finite standard flag by step 6.1. Conversely $H\circ(-)^{\#}$ sends a standard back to a standard: the transformation $E\mapsto\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*$ is involutive, and the unit and counit give its inverse. Induction on flag length thus restricts the equivalence precisely to the standard-flag categories. In category $\mathcal O$, $\zeta$ is semisimple; a finite generating set gives finitely many eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Choose a grading origin on each coset. Each standard has finite-dimensional graded components, because its finite Levi space has scalar $\zeta$-action and the graded pieces of $N$ are finite dimensional; the same holds for finite flags. Weight restriction and degree restriction therefore agree here. All $U$-morphisms preserve the actual $\zeta$-eigenvalues. Changing origins just shifts gradings, so the construction descends to the ungraded flag category using the $\zeta$-locally finite internal Hom. On outputs the eigenvalue cosets are shifted by $\gamma(\zeta)$ and negated by the principal dual; this is part of the construction, not an extra integrality assumption on highest weights.

**Reverse-column shifts.** The automorphism $c$ preserves the upper Borel and carries $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ to $\mathfrak p$. If the source Levi highest weight is $\lambda$, that of $E^*$ is $-w_{\bar J}\lambda$, so step 6.1 gives $\nu=-w_{\bar J}\lambda-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}$ before applying $c^*$. Pullback by $c$ sends a highest weight to $-w_0\nu$, giving the displayed weight map. A target block of length $r$ starting after $b$ coordinates has reversed source offset $b'=n-b-r$. The map $w_0w_{\bar J}$ preserves its position $k=1,\ldots,r$ inside the column. The value of $2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}$ on the source block is $n-2b'-r=b-b'$, hence the value of $2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}$ on the target block is $b-b'$. The source coordinate $a_i+b'+k-1$ is consequently transported to $a_i+b'+k-1+b-b'=a_i+i-1$. Thus $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))=\Delta(A)$ including the scalar trace-centre coordinate.

With $\rho_i=(n+1-2i)/2$, the shifted coordinate is $\lambda_{A,i}+\rho_i=a_i+(n-1)/2$. Reversing columns preserves its multiset, so corresponding source and target standards belong to matching central-character summands; extensions of standards in one summand remain in it, and hence so do the images under $\Psi$. At fixed total weight, each reversed-column prefix is the complementary suffix of the original reading; subtracting from the total changes the direction of each prefix-dominance inequality. This reverses the tableau order. Neither connectedness of a central summand nor an equivalence on arbitrary objects is used.

**Covariant equivalence.** Restricted BGG duality is exact and contravariant, sends target standards to costandards and preserves the target central summands. Composing it with the contravariant equivalence $\Psi$ gives the covariant exact equivalence $F=D\Psi$ and $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$. The label order reversal comes from step 8.1, whereas applying $D$ changes the variance and the kind of flag. This proves all the stated algebraic and filtered-category assertions with their restricted-Hom boundary.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, define the **standard** and **costandard** weight modules by

$$\Delta(\lambda)=M(\lambda),\qquad\nabla(\lambda)=D(M(\lambda)).$$

The Verma module is defined in [[def-verma-module]], and its restricted dual is defined in [[def-restricted-dual-of-a-weight-module]]. Under the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]] places $\nabla(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O$, so both displayed modules are objects of that category. These symbols impose no projectivity or highest-weight-category axiom.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every projective object
of $\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

More precisely, each projective cover $P(\mu)$ produced by
[[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]] is a direct summand of the
projective object $\operatorname{pr}_C(E\otimes M(\lambda))$ of
[[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]], which is a
direct summand of $E\otimes M(\lambda)$; a general projective object has
finite length, hence is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives,
each of which is a projective cover of its simple head.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every weight
$\lambda$ the restricted dual $I(\lambda)=D(P(\lambda))$ of the projective
cover is an injective object of $\mathcal O$
([[def-injective-object]]) and has a finite costandard ($\nabla$-)flag, with
multiplicities
$$(I(\lambda):\nabla(\mu))=(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]$$
in the sense of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
[[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]; the functor $D$ exchanges Verma flags of projectives
with costandard flags of injectives. Every injective object of $\mathcal O$
has a finite costandard flag: it is a finite direct sum of indecomposable
injectives, and $D$ induces a bijection between the indecomposable projectives
and the indecomposable injectives of $\mathcal O$
([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]); each
indecomposable injective is the dual of an indecomposable projective and hence
of the form $I(\lambda)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Every object of $\mathcal O$ has a finite composition series and is both Noetherian and Artinian. The length of zero is zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Restricted Chevalley duality is an exact contravariant equivalence $D:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{op}}$, with a natural isomorphism $D^2\cong\operatorname{id}$. It preserves each weight-space dimension, the formal character, and every simple composition multiplicity.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Flags, duality and the injective sequence.** Finite sums have flags by concatenation. Given $0\to X\to Y\to Z\to0$ with $X,Z$ standard-filtered, pull a flag of $Z$ back to $Y$ and precede it with the flag of $X$; this gives a standard flag of $Y$. Duality proves both claims for costandard flags and exchanges the two flag categories. Dualizing $0\to K_\lambda\to P_\lambda\to\Delta_\lambda\to0$ gives precisely $0\to\nabla_\lambda\to I_\lambda\to DK_\lambda\to0$, whose cokernel is costandard-filtered by labels strictly above $\lambda$. In particular this construction does not identify a general costandard with an injective envelope.

**All positive standard-costandard Ext groups.** The degree-one vanishing is [F1]. Suppose vanishing holds in degree $j-1$ for every pair of structural labels, where $j\ge2$. A finite standard flag of $K_\lambda$ and its long exact sequences give $\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}(K_\lambda,
abla_\mu)=0$. The projective sequence then gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{j}(\Delta_\lambda,
abla_\mu)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}(K_\lambda,
abla_\mu)=0$. Induction proves all positive degrees. Filtering the first variable now shows $\operatorname{Ext}^{j}(N,
abla_\mu)=0$ for any standard-filtered $N$; filtering the second variable gives the dual statement for costandard-filtered objects, and also vanishing between any standard-filtered and costandard-filtered pair.

**The maximal trace.** Choose a maximal label $\eta$ and put $e=e_\eta$. Since the standard-kernel sequence has no higher labels, $Ae=P_\eta=\Delta_\eta$. Every other standard is killed by $e$, while $\dim e\Delta_\eta=1$. An endomorphism of $\Delta_\eta$ is determined by its action on the generating top space, so $eAe=\operatorname{End}_A(Ae)^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathbb C$. For a standard-filtered $X$, the evaluation map $Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eX\to X$ is injective and its quotient is standard-filtered with no $\eta$ section. To prove this, induct on a chosen flag. If its last section is $\Delta_\eta$, the section splits off because $\Delta_\eta$ is projective. If its last section is another $\Delta_\lambda$, it is killed by $e$, so $eX=eX'$ for the preceding flag subobject $X'$ and the trace lies in $X'$; the induction quotient extends by $\Delta_\lambda$. This proves the claim in both cases, including identification with the canonical trace generated by $eX$.

**Multiplicity formulas.** For $0	o N'	o N	o\Delta_\lambda	o0$ with $N'$ standard-filtered, applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,
abla_\mu)$ and step 2.1 gives a short exact sequence of Hom spaces. Its dimension adds one precisely for $\lambda=\mu$. Inducting along a flag proves $(N:\Delta_\mu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,
abla_\mu)$ and independence of the flag. Duality gives $(M:
abla_\mu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\mu,M)$ for costandard-filtered $M$.

**The genuine heredity ideal.** Apply step 2.2 to each projective column $Ae_\lambda$ and sum the columns. The resulting injective evaluation map is multiplication $Ae\otimes_{eAe}eA\to A$, with image $J=AeA$. Thus $J\cong Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eA$, rather than $J=Ae$. It is projective on both sides: on the left it is a finite sum of $Ae$, and on the right a finite sum of $eA$. Moreover $e\operatorname{rad}(A)e=0$ since $eAe=\mathbb C$, so $J$ is a heredity ideal. Put $A'=A/J$. The finite $A'$-modules are exactly the $A$-modules killed by $e$, hence the Serre subcategory on $\Lambda\setminus\{\eta\}$. Its projective covers for $\lambda\ne\eta$ are $A'e_\lambda=Ae_\lambda/J e_\lambda$. By step 2.2 these have standard flags with all $\eta$ sections removed. The sequence onto $\Delta_\lambda$ has kernel $K_\lambda/J e_\lambda$: the trace $J e_\lambda$ lies in $K_\lambda$ because $e\Delta_\lambda=0$, and applying step 2.2 to $K_\lambda$ gives the required standard flag with the remaining strictly higher labels. Its simple top is still $L_\lambda$, so it is indeed the projective cover. Consequently $A'$ has the smaller highest-weight structure with unchanged standards $\Delta_\lambda$. Duality preserves this Serre subcategory and gives its injective envelopes and unchanged costandards $\nabla_\lambda$. Every injective $A'$-module is therefore costandard-filtered by these smaller labels. This establishes the quotient data needed for induction, without assuming the converse flag criterion.

**Normalized tilting uniqueness.** Suppose $X,X'$ are indecomposable tiltings with normalized inclusions $i:\Delta_\lambda\to X$ and $i':\Delta_\lambda\to X'$. Their cokernels are standard-filtered, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1(X/\Delta_\lambda,X')=0$. The Hom exact sequence extends $i'$ to $f:X\to X'$ with $fi=i'$; symmetrically obtain $g:X'\to X$ with $gi'=i$. Then $gf$ and $fg$ restrict to the identity on the common nonzero standard, and no positive power of either is zero. In a finite-dimensional endomorphism algebra of an indecomposable finite-length object, Fitting's decomposition makes every noninvertible endomorphism nilpotent. Hence both composites are invertible and $f$ is an isomorphism. The support of $\Delta_\lambda$ and of the lower-labelled quotient shows that $\lambda$ is the unique maximal support label. No existence or tilting classification was used in the flag-criterion argument.

**Ext1 implies every positive Ext degree.** Suppose $N$ satisfies $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(N,
abla_\lambda)=0$ for every label. Finite flags show $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(N,C)=0$ for every costandard-filtered $C$. More generally, if the groups vanish in degree $j-1$ against all costandards, they vanish in that degree against every costandard-filtered object. Apply this to $C_\lambda$ in the actual sequence $0	o
abla_\lambda	o I_\lambda	o C_\lambda	o0$ from step 1.1. Since $I_\lambda$ is injective, for $j\ge2$ dimension shifting gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,
abla_\lambda)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{j-1}_A(N,C_\lambda)=0$. Induction establishes all positive Ext vanishing, and filtering establishes $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,I')=0$ for every $j>0$ and every injective $A'$-module $I'$ from step 3.2, viewed as an $A$-module.

**Tor vanishing detected by injectives.** Choose a projective resolution $P_\bullet\to N$ by finite-dimensional projective $A$-modules. Each $A'\otimes_A P_i$ is projective over $A'$. For an injective $A'$-module $I'$, tensor-Hom adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet,I')$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_\bullet,I')$. The latter has zero cohomology in every positive degree by step 4.1. Because $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(-,I')$ is exact, the degree-$j$ cohomology of the former is $\operatorname{Hom}_{A'}(H_j(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet),I')$. Injectives detect nonzero finite-dimensional $A'$-modules: embed the semisimple socle of a finite module in a finite sum of the injective envelopes of the simples and extend the map by injectivity. Its kernel is zero because any nonzero finite-length submodule intersects that socle. Thus the full module embeds in such an injective cogenerator. It follows that $H_j(A'\otimes_A P_\bullet)=\operatorname{Tor}^A_j(A',N)=0$ for every $j>0$. This uses actual homology detection, not an assumed exactness of tensoring.

**The trace exact sequence and quotient induction.** Tensor $0	o J	o A	o A'	o0$ with $N$. By step 5.1 its Tor boundary vanishes, and step 3.2 identifies the result as $0	o Ae\otimes_{\mathbb C}eN	o N	o E	o0$, where $E=A'\otimes_A N$. The kernel is a finite sum of $\Delta_\eta$. Moreover $A'\otimes_A P_ ullet$ is a projective resolution of $E$ by step 5.1, and adjunction now gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_{A'}(E,
abla_\lambda)=\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(N,
abla_\lambda)=0$ for $j>0$, $\lambda
e\eta$. Induct on the number of labels, using the smaller highest-weight category constructed in step 3.2: $E$ is standard-filtered by the smaller labels. The base with no labels is the zero category; with one label the trace sequence itself is $N\cong\Delta_\eta\otimes eN$. Extension closure now makes $N$ standard-filtered. Together with steps 2.1 and 4.1 this proves both displayed standard-flag criteria, using either degree-one or all-positive-Ext vanishing.

**The dual criterion and direct summands.** Exact contravariant duality gives $\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(\Delta_\lambda,M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^j_A(DM,\nabla_\lambda)$ by reversing Yoneda extensions (and likewise in all degrees). The criterion for $DM$ in step 6.1 therefore gives the two costandard-flag criteria for $M$. If a flagged object is a finite direct sum, Ext groups of each summand are direct summands of its vanishing groups. The appropriate criterion shows every summand has the same kind of flag. Thus both flag categories, and their intersection of tilting objects, have all the stated closure properties.

**Lower ideals.** Let $X$ be a normalized tilting object at $\lambda$, and let $\Gamma$ be a lower ideal containing $\lambda$. Every composition label of $X$ lies below $\lambda$, so $X$ belongs to its Serre subcategory. Its standard flag uses labels in $\Gamma$; every costandard occurring in its costandard flag also has its own labelled simple as a composition factor of $X$, hence has label in $\Gamma$. These are the same standards and costandards in the truncated highest-weight category: iteratively removing maximal labels outside $\Gamma$ uses step 3.2. Thus $X$ remains the same normalized tilting there, and uniqueness follows from step 3.3. The closure, duality, multiplicity and full homological-criterion assertions have been established locally, including the genuine injective and heredity-ideal interfaces.

generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
$$\Phi(\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(E))\cong\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*).$$
The parabolic in this formula is unchanged.

(4) Let $c(X)=-w_0X^{\mathsf T}w_0$, which carries the upper Borel to itself and reverses the Levi blocks, and set $\Psi=c^*\Phi$. For a lower-bounded tableau shape set $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and use the concatenated ordinary highest-weight reading $a_i$, with each column read from top to bottom in strictly decreasing order, and $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$. The source reading is the reversed sequence of columns, without reversing positions within a column. Then
$$\Psi:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A).$$
This is an exact contravariant equivalence. It preserves the tableau label and the corresponding central-character summands, including the scalar central coordinate, and the reverse-column label order is opposite to the target order. More explicitly its weight map is
$$\lambda\longmapsto w_0w_{\bar J}\lambda+2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}.$$

(5) For restricted BGG transpose duality $D$, the composite $F=D\Psi$ is an exact covariant equivalence $\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$ with $F(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\nabla(A)$.

For category-$\mathcal O$ modules these constructions use finite weight spaces and the finite direct sum of $\zeta$-eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Internal homogeneous Hom becomes the $\zeta$-locally finite part of Hom, and the dual is the weight-restricted dual. No equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or unrestricted completed Hom spaces is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work in the type-$A$
root datum $W=S_n$ of the page's Hecke module and ordinary multiplicity
theorem. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]
with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of
[[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels
normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be
the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$,
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,\,ww_0}(1),$$
the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial attached to the
pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
Equivalently, put $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0\in{}^JW$. Then
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1).$$
This is the spherical family. The antispherical family instead governs the
genuine regular parabolic locally finite category with dominant labels;
changing to an opposite positive system does not identify the two families.
In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial
coefficients beyond the value at one occur.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every dominant
integral weight $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$, the character of the finite-dimensional
simple module $L(\lambda)$ is
$$\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=A(\lambda+\rho)\cdot A(\rho)^{-1}=\Bigl(\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}e^{w(\lambda+\rho)}\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(e^{\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})\Bigr),$$
the quotient being taken in the completed character ring $\mathcal R$ of
[[def-completed-formal-character-ring-for-downward-cones]], where
$A(\rho)$ is invertible with inverse
$e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-1}$
([[thm-weyl-denominator-identity]],
[[lem-geometric-series-invertibility-in-the-completed-character-ring]]). No
quotient of ordinary functions is intended before this formal cancellation is
justified.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] only for the quantum-bar suppliers. In a finite type-$A$ natural tensor space, write $s$ for the source parameter, $a w$ for the right place action, $w_a$ for the shortest sorting permutation, $d_a=w_a^{-1}$, $K$ for the stabilizer of the weakly increasing sorted tuple, $w_K$ for its longest element, and $w_0$ for the full longest permutation. Let $L_b=\sum_a U_{a,b}(s)M_a$ be the positive-source ordinary-bar chart and $M_b=\sum_a D_{a,b}(s)L_a$ its inverse. Then
$$U_{a,b}(s)=(-s)^{\ell(w_b)-\ell(w_a)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_az,w_b}(s^{-2}),$$
$$D_{a,b}(s)=s^{\ell(w_b)-\ell(w_a)}P_{d_bw_0,d_aw_0}(s^{-2}).$$
Coefficients vanish outside the indicated Bruhat intervals. For decreasing-column wedge tensors in either factor order, the ordinary-bar embedding is
$$\iota(M_B)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}M_{a(C)},\qquad \iota(L_A)=L_{a(A)}.$$
Consequently the wedge inverse coefficient is
$$d_{A,B}(s)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}D_{a(A),a(C)}(s).$$
Here $\ell(B,C)$ is the number of within-column adjacent swaps from the decreasing reading. These identities are independent of category $\mathcal O$ and of linkage or simple-label identification.

derivations.claim: **The actual normalized projective image.** Fix one finite highest-weight central summand and a label $B$, and put $X(B)=\Psi(P^{\bar p}(B))$. The source projective has its highest-weight exact sequence $0\to\bar K(B)\to P^{\bar p}(B)\to\bar\Delta(B)\to0$, with a finite standard flag on $\bar K(B)$ using strictly higher source labels. Exact contravariance of $\Psi$ gives $0\to\Delta(B)\to X(B)\to\Psi\bar K(B)\to0$. Order reversal makes the quotient standard-filtered by labels strictly below $B$. Thus this is an actual normalized bottom inclusion, and $\Delta(B)$ occurs once. The endomorphism ring of $X(B)$ is opposite to the local ring of its source projective cover, so $X(B)$ is indecomposable.

**The CWZ parameter, coproduct and ordered labels.** In the two-wedge convention of Cheng–Wang–Zhang, write $q$ for their parameter and $K_a$ for their toral generator. The exact transport to [F4] is $q\mapsto s^{-1}$, $K_a\mapsto D_a^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$, and $K_f\mapsto M_f$ for the same two decreasing columns in the same left/right order. Their natural eigenvalue $q^{\delta_{ab}}$ becomes $s^{-\delta_{ab}}$, the eigenvalue of $D_a^{-1}$. The toral relations and the $E/F$ commutator agree because both numerator and denominator of the toral fraction reverse sign. Their coproducts are $\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes K_{a+1}K_a^{-1}$ and $\Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+K_aK_{a+1}^{-1}\otimes F_a$; these become exactly $1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$ and $F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a$ of [F4]. Thus reciprocal parameter substitution alone is accompanied by toral inversion, and no reversal of tensor factors or tableau entries is used. The quantum Serre coefficients are unchanged under reciprocation, and the two bars agree on coefficients and generators: both fix $E_a,F_a$ and invert the torus. The displayed source coproduct and ordered factor actions are those of [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]. The ordered wedge basis has coefficient-one adjacent-entry replacement actions, so it identifies the elementary wedge factors; their relation on unordered wedges becomes $-s$, consistently with this transport. A swap of exclusive left $b>$ right $a$ gives a strictly smaller label in both orders, since the left prefix changes by the positive root $\delta_a-\delta_b$. Consequently the CWZ positive-$q$ triangular chart maps to the negative-$s^{-1}$ chart of $T$, not to the positive-$s$ chart of $L$.

**Tilting and an actual normalized dual flag.** For an extension $0\to X(B)\to Z\to\Delta(A)\to0$, the middle object is standard-filtered by extension closure. Inverting $\Psi$ turns it into an extension with the opposite projective as quotient, which splits. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(A),X(B))=0$ for every $A$, and the criterion of [F1] makes $X(B)$ costandard-filtered and therefore tilting. The object $DX(B)$ is also tilting and indecomposable; duality fixes simple classes, so all its composition labels are $\le B$ and $[DX(B):L(B)]=1$. In the lower highest-weight ideal of labels $\le B$, $\Delta(B)$ is the maximal-labelled projective. The maximal standard trace proved in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] injects $\Delta(B)$ into the standard-filtered $DX(B)$ with quotient standard-filtered by strictly smaller labels: its multiplicity space has dimension $[DX(B):L(B)]=1$. Thus the dual has an actual normalized bottom-standard sequence. Uniqueness of such indecomposable tiltings in [F1] gives $X(B)\cong DX(B)$. This normalization uses the proved maximal trace and does not follow from exchanging the kinds of flags alone.

**Local three-case calculation in the corrected chart.** For a column $S$ write $n_S(a)=\mathbf1_{a\in S}$ and omit a replacement term if it would collide. The transported coproduct gives $E_aM_{L,R}=M_{L,R(a+1\mapsto a)}+s^{n_R(a)-n_R(a+1)}M_{L(a+1\mapsto a),R}$ and $F_aM_{L,R}=M_{L(a\mapsto a+1),R}+s^{-n_L(a)+n_L(a+1)}M_{L,R(a\mapsto a+1)}$. Match exclusive pairs by increasing positive distance, deleting matched endpoints, and call the resulting set $\Sigma_f^+$. Distinct pairs at the same distance cannot share an endpoint, so this prescription is unambiguous. Choose the smallest left value $b=a+1$ that is a matched endpoint. If $a$ is absent on the left, let $h$ lower this $b$ to $a$ and apply $F_a$. If $a$ is present on the left, it must also occur on the right: otherwise its distance to the right partner of $b$ would be smaller, forcing it to be a matched left endpoint contrary to the choice of $b$. In this case let $h$ raise that right $a$ to $b$ and apply $E_a$. The matching rules then give three cases: when the lower left neighbor $a$ is shared, its pair endpoint in $h$ moves from $b$ to $a$ and all other pairs persist; when $a$ is absent on both sides the pair set persists with that endpoint lowered; when $a$ occurs only on the right, $h$ loses precisely the distance-one pair $(b,a)$. For every subset of the remaining pairs, the two displayed action formulas have coefficient one in the first two cases: if a selected pair moves the active letter to the other column, the two relevant occupation numbers agree. In the last case both columns of $h$ contain $a$ and neither contains $b$, so $F_aM_{h_\Sigma}=M_{f_\Sigma}+s^{-1}M_{f_{\Sigma\cup\{(b,a)\}}}$. No wedge sorting sign enters, since an adjacent integer replacement either preserves its sorted position or is zero on collision.

**The opposite BGG coefficient identity.** From the tilting nature and maximal support of $X(B)$, every multiplicity can be computed as $(X(B):\Delta(A))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(X(B),\nabla(A))$. Applying the exact contravariant $\Psi$ to the finite standard flag of $\bar P(B)$ reverses its order but preserves the multiplicities of its corresponding standard sections. Opposite BGG reciprocity therefore gives $(X(B):M(A))=(\bar P(B):\bar M(A))=[\bar M(A):\bar L(B)]$, the opposite parabolic composition coefficient.

**Bar-fixed pair formula and coefficient.** The predecessor procedure in step 2.2 terminates: $\sum L-\sum R$ decreases by one at each predecessor, all entries remain in the finite interval between the original smallest and largest entries, and both column sizes are fixed. At its terminal tuple there is no positive exclusive pair; in the fixed union/intersection fiber this is the unique minimal label, so its monomial is fixed by the triangular bar of [F4]. Apply the recorded $E_a,F_a$ in reverse predecessor order; they are bar-fixed. The subset calculation of step 2.2 proves inductively that the resulting bar-fixed vector is $U_f=\sum_{\Sigma\subseteq\Sigma_f^+}s^{-|\Sigma|}M_{f_\Sigma}$. The empty subset gives $M_f$, every nonempty subset gives a lower label, and disjoint exclusive endpoints make distinct subsets give distinct tableaux. Thus $U_f$ has precisely the negative-chart triangular condition of $T_f$, and uniqueness in [F4] gives $U_f=T_f$. In particular every single greedy-pair coefficient is $s^{-1}$ and specializes to $1$. This supplies the local proof in the correct chart; it does not identify a positive-$s$ fixed vector with the negative-chart canonical family.

**The independent tensor/wedge bridge and opposite flag.** Apply [[lem-finite-type-a-tensor-hecke-bars-and-complementary-coefficient-charts]] before making any categorical identification. Its tensor generators act at $v=s^{-1}$, its positive chart transports to the sign module by $G_i=-H_i$ at $v=s$, and its complementary representative is $w_Kd(A)w_0$. The proved inverse tensor coefficient is $s^{\ell(w_C)-\ell(w_A)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(s^{-2})$, so its value at $1$ is exactly the ordinary singular composition number in [F3]. The primitive ordinary-bar exterior embedding has coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}$ on column permutations $C$ and sends the wedge $L_A$ to the ambient $L_{a(A)}$. Its signed inverse formula at $1$ therefore agrees term for term with finite Levi Weyl cancellation of the genuine generalized-standard character: $d_{A,B}(1)=[\Delta(B):L(A)]$. This uses character injectivity, and it keeps the equal-entry stabilizer separate from the column Levi. The helper proves the same transport for reversed factors; hence $\widetilde d_{B,A}(1)=[\bar\Delta(A):\bar L(B)]$. At $s=1$ the ordinary tensor bar matrix is the identity (each adjacent exchange has correction $s^{-1}-s=0$), so the reverse form of [F4] has monomial Gram matrix $I$. The identity $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$ now says that the monomial coefficient matrix of $T$ is the transpose inverse of the coefficient matrix of $\widetilde L$, namely $\widetilde d^{\mathsf T}$. Thus the coefficient of $M(A)$ in $T_B$ at $1$ is $\widetilde d_{B,A}(1)=[\bar\Delta(A):\bar L(B)]=(X(B):\Delta(A))$ by step 3.1. All sign, longest-element and reverse-factor transports have been proved independently of this linkage conclusion.

**Isolation of adjacent columns in a larger tensor.** If two tableaux have the same entries outside two adjacent columns, every tableau in the Bruhat interval between them has the same outer prefix weights, since dominance is antisymmetric on fixed total weight; parenthesizing the pair as one tensor factor, a positive transfer across an outer boundary strictly changes a prefix weight in the positive cone and cannot be cancelled by further positive transfers. Hence the bar submatrix and, by triangular correction, the canonical coefficient between the two labelled monomials equal the two-column values of step 3.2.

**Genuine edges at $1$.** Specializing step 4.2 at $s=1$, a greedy-pair swap gives $(X(B):M(A))=1$ for the two labels connected by the swap: the corresponding standard factor occurs with multiplicity $1$ in the indecomposable tilting object $X(B)$. Since an indecomposable finite-length object cannot have composition factors in two different linkage blocks, and $M(A)$ has simple head $L(A)$ while the actual $\Delta(B)$ section of $X(B)$ supplies $L(B)$ as a composition factor, the labels $A$ and $B$ lie in the same actual linkage block. Opposite BGG gives $[\bar M(A):\bar L(B)]=1$, and $\bar M(A)$ has head $\bar L(A)$, so the same edge connects the opposite labels.

**Connectivity of the binary tableau fiber.** Identify a tableau with the $0/1$ incidence matrix recording which entry values occur in each column; its row margins are entry multiplicities and its column margins are the heights $n_j$. The symmetric difference of two matrices with the same margins is a union of alternating cycles in the bipartite graph, and a cycle of length $2k$ is flipped by a chord: if the chord entry is $0$ flip the smaller four-cycle first and then the remaining shorter cycle, if it is $1$ flip the complementary shorter cycle first and then the four-cycle; the chord is restored and exactly the original cycle is flipped. Induction on the cycle length gives a sequence of valid $2\times2$ switches connecting any two matrices with the same margins.

**Reduction of distant switches.** Reduce a switch of entries $a,b$ between nonadjacent columns $S,U$ through the next intermediate column $T$. If $T$ contains only $a$ or only $b$, two switches with shorter column distance restore $T$ and effect the $S/U$ switch. If $T$ contains both, then $T\setminus S$ contains $b$ and, since $|S|\ge|T|$, some $c\in S\setminus T$ with $c\ne a$; use $c\leftrightarrow b$ on $S,T$, then $a\leftrightarrow b$ on $T,U$, then $a\leftrightarrow c$ on $S,T$. If $T$ contains neither, then $U\setminus T$ contains $b$ and, since $|T|\ge|U|$, some $c\in T\setminus U$; use $c\leftrightarrow b$ on $T,U$, then $a\leftrightarrow b$ on $S,T$, then $a\leftrightarrow c$ on $T,U$. Every step is a valid binary switch preserving the margins, and induction on the column distance reduces to adjacent columns. These cardinal comparisons use exactly the original sorted heights $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$.

**Adjacent fibers connect through coefficient-$1$ edges.** Every adjacent two-column switch has both endpoints in one union/intersection fiber of the pair of columns. Repeatedly swapping any greedy positive pair strictly lowers the inversion order of the tuple, and the process terminates at the unique configuration in which all left-exclusive values precede all right-exclusive values. Hence the endpoints are connected through the canonical coefficient-$1$ edges of step 3.2 and step 5.1.
