Hence both genuine type-$A$ tableau central summands are single linkage blocks, including repeated-entry singular ambient characters; no future higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem and no bare Bruhat-cover connectivity assertion is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published category-$\mathcal O$ theory. Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard
parabolic of
[[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with
reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$, nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$ and Weyl
group $W_J$; the ambient category is $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]
with standard objects the Verma modules [[def-verma-module]].

**(1) Dominance for the Levi.** A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant**
if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all
$\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular
$\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$; see
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]] for the ambient
notion).

**(2) Generalized Verma modules.** For a $\mathfrak p$-dominant $\lambda$ let
$E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained
from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight
$\lambda$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero. Define the **generalized Verma module**

$$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$

**(3) The parabolic category.** The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely
generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which
$U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely, that is, on which every vector lies
in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule; equivalently, every vector
lies in a finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak l_J$-submodule and is annihilated by a power of $\mathfrak u_J$
(local finiteness for the nilpotent $\mathfrak u_J$).

The following structural facts are part of the definition; the arguments are
given in the Remarks.

**(4) Generalized Vermas lie in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.** For each
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$, $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is an
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ with highest weight $\lambda$, and the
natural surjection $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$
exhibits $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ as the largest quotient of the Verma
module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(5) Simples.** The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly
the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral
([[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]).

**(6) Serre property.** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects,
quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$; in particular it is an abelian
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ stable under finite direct sums.

**(7) Costandard objects.** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ put
$\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, the restricted
dual of [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]].
These are the **costandard objects** of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; each is
naturally a submodule of the ordinary dual Verma $D M(\lambda)$. They need not
be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published root-space and $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ suppliers. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a
finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra
$\mathfrak h$, root system $\Phi$
([[thm-the-root-set-is-a-reduced-crystallographic-root-system]],
[[thm-root-space-decomposition-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra]],
[[thm-root-spaces-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra-are-one-dimensional]]),
positive system $\Phi^+$ with base of simple roots
$\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$
([[def-positive-system-and-base-of-simple-roots]],
[[def-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]]), and let $J$ be a
subset of the simple indices $\{1,\dots,r\}$. Write $\Phi_J$ for the root
subsystem spanned by the simple roots indexed by $J$,
$$\Phi_J=\Phi\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\alpha_j:j\in J\},$$
and let $H_j=h_{\alpha_j}\in\mathfrak h$ be the coroot of $\alpha_j$
([[def-coroot-of-a-lie-algebra-root]] via
[[def-killing-dual-vector-of-a-root]]). Put
$$\mathfrak h_J=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{H_j:j\in J\},\qquad \mathfrak z_J=\{h\in\mathfrak h:\alpha_j(h)=0\text{ for all }j\in J\},$$
and define the following subspaces of $\mathfrak g$, where $\mathfrak g_\alpha$
is the root space of $\alpha$
([[thm-root-space-decomposition-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra]]):

$$\mathfrak s_J=\mathfrak h_J\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak l_J=\mathfrak s_J\oplus\mathfrak z_J=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,$$
$$\mathfrak u_J=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Phi^+\smallsetminus\Phi_J^+}\mathfrak g_\beta,\qquad \mathfrak v_J=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Phi^-\smallsetminus\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\beta,\qquad \mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J .$$

Here $\Phi_J^\pm=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^\pm$ and $\Phi^\pm$ are the positive and
negative roots with $\mathfrak n^\pm$, $\mathfrak b$ as in
[[def-positive-and-negative-nilpotent-subalgebras-and-borel-subalgebra]]. The
construction depends only on the positive system and on $J$. The following
structural facts are part of the definition (proofs and references in the
Remarks; $\operatorname{rad}$ and $\operatorname{nilrad}$ are those of
[[def-radical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]] and
[[def-nilradical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]]).

**(1) Decomposition of the Cartan.** $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak h_J\oplus\mathfrak z_J$
and $\dim\mathfrak h_J=|J|$, so $\dim\mathfrak z_J=r-|J|$.

**(2) The semisimple part.** $\mathfrak s_J$ is a Lie subalgebra of
$\mathfrak g$; it is semisimple, and its root system with respect to the
Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h_J$ is $\Phi_J$, with positive system
$\Phi_J^+$ and Weyl group $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle\le W$
([[def-weyl-group-of-a-root-system]],
[[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]).

**(3) The reductive Levi algebra.** $\mathfrak l_J$ is a Lie subalgebra with
root system $\Phi_J$ relative to $\mathfrak h$; it is reductive as in
[[def-simple-semisimple-and-reductive-lie-algebras]], with center
$\mathfrak z_J$ and derived algebra $[\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak l_J]=\mathfrak s_J$;
$\mathfrak h$ is a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak l_J$ and the Weyl group of
$(\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak h)$ is $W_J$. The algebra $\mathfrak l_J$ need not
be semisimple: its center $\mathfrak z_J$ is nonzero as soon as $J\ne\{1,\dots,r\}$.

**(4) Parabolic and radicals.** $\mathfrak l_J$, $\mathfrak u_J$, $\mathfrak v_J$
and $\mathfrak p_J$ are Lie subalgebras
([[prop-brackets-of-root-spaces]]); $\mathfrak u_J$ is an ideal of
$\mathfrak p_J$, $\mathfrak l_J$ stabilizes $\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathfrak v_J$,
and $\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\ltimes\mathfrak u_J$ is a semidirect product
([[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]]). Moreover
$\operatorname{nilrad}(\mathfrak p_J)=\mathfrak u_J$ and
$$\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak p_J)=\mathfrak z_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J .$$
Consequently $[\mathfrak p_J,\mathfrak p_J]=\mathfrak s_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$
and the quotient $\mathfrak p_J/\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak p_J)\cong\mathfrak s_J$
is semisimple: in the sense of
[[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]], $\mathfrak s_J$ is a semisimple
Levi factor of $\mathfrak p_J$ and $\mathfrak l_J$ is the reductive complement
to the nilradical. The parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$ contains $\mathfrak b$ and
$\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\alpha$,
the span of the negative root spaces of $\Phi_J$; for $J=\varnothing$ one has
$\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b$, and for $J=\{1,\dots,r\}$ one has
$\mathfrak l_J=\mathfrak s_J=\mathfrak g$ and
$\mathfrak u_J=\mathfrak v_J=0$.

**(5) The positive grading.** There exists $\zeta\in\mathfrak z_J$ with
$\alpha_j(\zeta)=0$ for $j\in J$ and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ for $i\notin J$. With
respect to $\operatorname{ad}(\zeta)$ every root space $\mathfrak g_\beta$ has
weight $\beta(\zeta)$, so:

* $\mathfrak l_J$ has degree $0$ (all of $\Phi_J$ vanishes on $\zeta$);
* $\mathfrak u_J$ has strictly positive integral degrees
  $\beta(\zeta)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$;
* $\mathfrak v_J$ has strictly negative integral degrees.

In particular $\mathfrak u_J$ is nilpotent by this positive grading, and both
$\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathfrak v_J$ have finite-dimensional fixed-degree
slices of their PBW algebras:
$\dim U(\mathfrak u_J)_d<\infty$ and $\dim U(\mathfrak v_J)_d<\infty$ for
every $d\in\mathbb Z$ ([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]).

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The simple objects of $\mathcal O$ are exactly the modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, and $L(\lambda)\cong L(\mu)$ if and only if $\lambda=\mu$. Simplicity here excludes zero.

Every finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak g$-module is a cyclic highest-weight module whose highest weight is dominant integral, and for each dominant integral weight

$$\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^r m_i\omega_i \qquad (m_i\in \mathbb N_0),$$

there exists, up to isomorphism, a unique finite-dimensional simple module $L(\lambda)$ with highest weight $\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a chosen positive-root system and corresponding Borel, Weyl group $W$, and half-sum $\rho$ of positive roots. Let $\chi_\lambda$ and $\chi_\mu$ be the central characters obtained from highest weights $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ for this Borel. Then

$$\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu \quad \text{if and only if} \quad \mu\in W\cdot \lambda,$$

where $W\cdot \lambda:=\{w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho : w\in W\}$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Let $\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in I}$ be the simple roots of the chosen positive system and write $Q^+=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$ and $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$. Let $W$ be the Weyl group of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]] and let $\rho$ be the Weyl vector of [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]]; for $w\in W$ set $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The **BGG category $\mathcal O$** is the full subcategory of left $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules $M$ satisfying all three conditions: $M$ is finitely generated; $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak h^*}M_\mu$ where $M_\mu=\{v:hv=\mu(h)v\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\}$; and $U(\mathfrak n^+)v$ is finite dimensional for each $v\in M$. Its morphisms are all $\mathfrak g$-linear maps. The zero module is included, generated by the empty set. The enveloping and triangular conventions are those of [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] and [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]].

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, the **Verma module** is the induced
$\mathfrak g$-module

$$M(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda,$$

where $U(\mathfrak g)$ is the quotient algebra of
[[def-universal-enveloping-algebra-as-a-tensor-quotient]] and
$\mathbb C_\lambda$ is [[def-one-dimensional-borel-module-of-weight-lambda]].
Write $v_\lambda:=1\otimes c_\lambda$.  Thus $M(\lambda)$ is the quotient of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ by the left ideal generated by $x$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$
and $h-\lambda(h)$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$; in particular,
$\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$ and $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For the Fock shape
$n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$ (the original nonincreasing-charge hypothesis) and any
admitted integral entry multiset, the genuine $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ parabolic
central summand labelled by its strict-column tableaux is a **single linkage
block**. The same holds for its reverse-column/reversed-Levi counterpart.
This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses
actual indecomposable generalized standards and locally constructed tiltings:
adjacent-column positive exclusive-pair canonical coefficients specialize
to $1$, so those labels lie in a common actual linkage block, and these edges
connect the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber. No future
higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem is imported.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
$$\Phi(\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(E))\cong\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*).$$
The parabolic in this formula is unchanged.

(4) Let $c(X)=-w_0X^{\mathsf T}w_0$, which carries the upper Borel to itself and reverses the Levi blocks, and set $\Psi=c^*\Phi$. For a lower-bounded tableau shape set $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and use the concatenated ordinary highest-weight reading $a_i$, with each column read from top to bottom in strictly decreasing order, and $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$. The source reading is the reversed sequence of columns, without reversing positions within a column. Then
$$\Psi:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A).$$
This is an exact contravariant equivalence. It preserves the tableau label and the corresponding central-character summands, including the scalar central coordinate, and the reverse-column label order is opposite to the target order. More explicitly its weight map is
$$\lambda\longmapsto w_0w_{\bar J}\lambda+2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}.$$

(5) For restricted BGG transpose duality $D$, the composite $F=D\Psi$ is an exact covariant equivalence $\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$ with $F(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\nabla(A)$.

For category-$\mathcal O$ modules these constructions use finite weight spaces and the finite direct sum of $\zeta$-eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Internal homogeneous Hom becomes the $\zeta$-locally finite part of Hom, and the dual is the weight-restricted dual. No equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or unrestricted completed Hom spaces is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Levi dominance and the shifted multiset.** Read each strict column from top to bottom, as stipulated for the ordinary highest-weight tuple. Then $a_j>a_{j+1}$ within each Levi block and the integral difference is at least one. Consequently $\lambda_{A,j}-\lambda_{A,j+1}=a_j-a_{j+1}-1\ge0$, so $\lambda_A$ is weakly dominant and integral for the Levi. Consecutive ground entries may give equality of these highest-weight coordinates, which is allowed. This ordinary tuple follows the same normally ordered column reading. Therefore $L(A)$ and $M(A)$ are genuine objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ by [F1]. Because $\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$ has total sum $0$, the $j$-th shifted coordinate is $\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+(n-1)/2$, so the shifted-coordinate multiset differs from the entry multiset by the common scalar $(n-1)/2$; by [F2] this multiset together with the trace-centre scalar determines the central character, with no undeclared full-staircase shift.

**The block and its labels.** Fix an admitted entry multiset $\alpha$; its shifted-coordinate multiset gives one central character, and the simple modules $L(A)$ of that central character form exactly the labels $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha$. The induced modules $M(A)$ are the generalized standards of the block, the projectives $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$ exist by [F1], and BGG reciprocity and restricted duality hold blockwise because they are inherited from the ambient parabolic category.

**Filtered and Grothendieck structure.** By [F1] every object of the block has finite length with simple factors among the $L(A)$, and the projective covers have finite $M(A)$-flags; the simple and standard classes are bases of the block Grothendieck group with the stated unitriangular character matrix. By [F3] the block is a single linkage block, so all its labels are connected by actual indecomposable-tilting edges, including repeated-entry singular central characters; the direct sum over the admitted multisets is $\mathcal O^\Lambda$.

**Opposite blocks.** Reversing the Levi order and reading tableaux by columns in the reverse direction swaps the blocks and reverses the prefix order of the labels; by [F4] the reversed labels are the same tableaux with reversed column readings, and the corresponding central characters are the reversed-coordinate multisets. This is the opposite-block dictionary.

derivations.claim: **Coset representatives.** Put $b=a(A)w_A$, the weakly increasing tuple. The permutations sorting $a(A)$ are exactly $w_AK$: indeed $a(A)w=b$ if and only if $b(w_A^{-1}w)=b$. Choosing $w_A$ shortest in this coset makes it minimal-right modulo $K$, and inversion makes $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ minimal-left. The column Levi subgroup $J$ permutes positions within each column; it is generally different from $K$, which permutes the equal-entry positions of $b$.

**Explicit reciprocal action and signed chart.** The independent construction [[lem-finite-type-a-tensor-hecke-bars-and-complementary-coefficient-charts]] gives, at $v=s^{-1}$, the actual action $M_aH_i=M_{as_i}$ on an ascent, $sM_a$ on an equality, and $M_{as_i}+(s-s^{-1})M_a$ on a descent. The cyclic sorted tuple is fixed by the source bar and has stabilizer character $s$, so this is the trivial-induced tensor module with its induced bar, including equal entries. Changing generators to $G_i=-H_i$ gives the algebra at $v=s$, the sign character $-s$, and standard vector $n_{d(A)}=(-1)^{\ell(d(A))}M_A$. Thus the source-positive tensor fixed vector is the sign canonical vector multiplied by its leading sign. The helper's alternating-sum calculation and the inversion anti-involution of the Hecke algebra yield its coefficient $p_{A,B}(-s)$ and precisely the polynomial $p_{A,B}(s)$ stated. This resolves the bar sign by an explicit generator and standard-vector transport.

**Ordinary-bar exterior embedding and complementary spherical chart.** The same helper constructs the primitive exterior vector of a decreasing column as $\sum_C(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}M_{a(C)}$. Its adjacent generator eigenvalue is $-s^{-1}$, quantum replacements preserve its coefficient-one normalization, and quasi-$R$ naturality identifies its ordinary bar with the wedge-factor bar. Product embeddings therefore have the displayed independent column sum, with leading coefficient one and positive-source corrections; triangular uniqueness gives $\iota(L_A)=L_{a(A)}$. Independently, the reverse-position chart has representative $c_A=w_Kd(A)w_0$. The actual bilinear normalization is $(M_a,\psi M_b^*)=\delta_{ab}$; symmetry and complementary positive/negative polynomial congruences give $U^{\mathsf T}\bar V=I$. Hence the inverse tensor chart is $D_{a,b}=\bar V_{b,a}=s^{\ell(w_b)-\ell(w_a)}P_{d(b)w_0,d(a)w_0}(s^{-2})$. Expanding the primitive exterior sum in this inverse chart proves the wedge inverse formula, including its signs and all repeated-entry indices.

**Support and inverse matrix.** Triangularity of the ordinary KL basis and the sign alternation give $p_{A,A}=1$ and $p_{A,B}=0$ unless $A\le B$; the complementary chart $d$ defined by $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}L_A$ is the inverse unitriangular matrix through $p(-s)$, as in the definition of the Fock bases of [F3].

**The mixed composition matrix.** Step 1.3 gives $D_{a(A),a(C)}(1)=P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$ and $d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}D_{a(A),a(C)}(1)$. Finite Levi Weyl characters and PBW give $\mathrm{ch}\,M(B)=\sum_C(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}\mathrm{ch}\,M_{\mathrm{ord}}(C)$, with $C$ running over independent column permutations. Comparing coefficients of simple characters, which are linearly independent in the finite block, gives the same signed sum. Therefore $[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)$ with the displayed mixed parabolic matrix. The column subgroup and the equal-entry subgroup are used at separate stages, so repeated entries cause no conflation of sign and spherical families.

citations.quote:
Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]] with
source parameter $s$.

(1) For a finite interval $[k,r]$, the normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_d}$, $i_1>\cdots>i_d$, $i_a\in[k,r]$, form an
integral basis of the fundamental wedge $\Lambda^d V$, where the wedge is the
antisymmetrized tensor word with coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$ over the
symmetric group; the span is primitive over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$. This does
not assert that the antisymmetrizer embedding into the raw tensor power is based
in the library's lower $q_0$ chart.

(2) The column monomials $M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, form a basis of the
higher-level Fock module $F(\Lambda)$ on every finite cut, with the weights
$\mathrm{wt}(A)$ of the Definition.

(3) Let a finite interval $[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ be a **cut** containing all
entries of a given monomial (upper cut), and $k-1<k$ a further lower residue;
the **lower-cut embedding** $\iota_k$ appends the common bottom entry $k-1$ to
each of the $l$ columns, $\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$. The embeddings are
injective, compatible with the monomial action, and their compatible direct
limit over shrinking lower cuts and growing upper cuts is the full bounded or
semi-infinite Fock module of the Definition.

(4) Every generator acts by finitely many box moves and shifts weight spaces;
each fixed-weight space of $F(\Lambda)$ is finite dimensional. A merely
lower-bounded infinite interval need not give finite-dimensional fundamental
factors; all finite-Cartan statements are applied on finite cuts.

Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in root dominance for every $j<l$: the difference of the two prefix weights
is a nonnegative integral combination of the simple roots $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$. This is the coordinate-prefix criterion verified below, and
is defined for these weight vectors rather than only for partitions
([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]); then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

For any finite sequence of based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space category $O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the field tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\text{composite factor bars})$, built from the normalized intertwiner $\Theta$ of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], is well defined, semilinear, $U$- and bar-compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations; all root-height sums are vectorwise finite.

This field assertion holds for arbitrary based pairs and does not imply integral action. Its integral and based assertion holds for exactly the admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]: highest-first or first $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest or $C_{\mathrm{low}}$ second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients and direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs and products in finite Cartan type. For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently proved integral $\Theta$ action, not on field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.

In these cases: $\Psi$ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice; its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal $1$; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors modulo $q$, with corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; they form a genuine $A$-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple; the $q=0$ tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], and the infinity chart is $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$, not an asserted bar containment in $L_0$, since semilinearity sends $q$ to $q^{-1}$. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. Exact based integral and bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-$R$ braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action; the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter.

**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module that is integrable, has finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight set contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).

(i) **Splitting along the top isotypic part.** Let $\lambda$ be a maximal weight of $M$, put $N_0:=U_q(\mathfrak g)M_\lambda$ and let $N_1$ be the sum of the remaining simple constituents, so that $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$. Then $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$, $B=\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_0)/q(L\cap N_0)\bigr)\sqcup\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_1)/q(L\cap N_1)\bigr)$, and both pairs are crystal bases of $N_0$ and $N_1$.

(ii) **Uniqueness.** There is a locally weight-finite indexed family $(\lambda_j)_{j\in J}$ in $P^+$ and an isomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules $\Phi:M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{j\in J}V(\lambda_j)$ with $\Phi(L)=\bigoplus_j\mathcal L(\lambda_j)$ and $\Phi$ inducing a bijection $B\to\bigsqcup_j\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ of crystals. The multiset $\{\lambda_j:j\in J\}$ is the multiset of highest weights of the simple integrable constituents of $M$: the number of $j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda$ equals the multiplicity $[M:V(\lambda)]$.

(iii) **Components.** Through $\Phi$ the connected components of the crystal $B$ are exactly the canonical highest weight crystals $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$; each component has a unique highest weight element $b$, of dominant weight $\lambda$, and equals the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]. In particular the crystal graph of any crystal basis of $M$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$, and no other highest weight elements occur.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and used to obtain the decomposition of $M$ into simple integrable highest weight modules from [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], which selects a maximal independent family of simple submodules simultaneously. It also permits simultaneous choices of lifts of the finite residue bases in the possibly infinite family of top spaces. After those choices, each lattice and crystal argument is finite and choice-free. No incompatible-axiom branch is used, and no global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness is assumed. The index set $J$ need not be finite in affine or indefinite type; local weight finiteness means only finitely many summands contribute to any fixed label-weight space.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with Borel subalgebra
$U_q^{\ge0}=U_q^0U_q^+$ and negative half $U_q^-$
([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). Fix
$\lambda\in P$ and let $\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)$ be the
**Borel character module** on which $K_h$ acts by the scalar
$q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}$ and every $E_i$ acts as $0$ (the character is a
well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism
$\chi_\lambda\colon U_q^{\ge0}\to\mathbb Q(q)$, Verification, step 1.1). The
**quantum Verma module** is the induced module

$$M(\lambda):=U_q(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U_q^{\ge0}}\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda,$$

a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module, with distinguished vector
$v_\lambda:=1\otimes1$ ([[def-quotient-ring]] for the quotient/induction
conventions).

Then (Verification, steps 2.1 and 3.1):

(i) $M(\lambda)$ carries the **canonical $P$-label grading**
$M(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M(\lambda)_\mu$ with
$M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}=U_q^-[-\nu]v_\lambda$ for $\nu\in Q_+$ and
$M(\lambda)_\mu=0$ otherwise; each $M(\lambda)_\mu$ is finite dimensional
(there are only finitely many words in the $F_i$ of a given root degree), and
$M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ is the highest line. With this
grading $M(\lambda)$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and $v_\lambda$ is a highest
weight vector: $K_hv_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v_\lambda$,
$E_iv_\lambda=0$, $M(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.

(ii) (Universal property) For every left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $V$ and every
$v\in V$ with $K_hv=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v$ and $E_iv=0$ for all $h,i$
there is a unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $M(\lambda)\to V$ with
$v_\lambda\mapsto v$; if $V=U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is cyclic, this map is
surjective. When $V$ is a $P$-graded type-one module and $v\in V_\lambda$, the
map is grading-preserving.

(iii) The sum $N(\lambda)$ of all proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$ is a
proper graded submodule, and

$$L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$$

is the **simple highest weight quotient**: it has no nonzero proper graded
submodule, and it is the unique simple graded quotient of $M(\lambda)$ up to
isomorphism ([[def-submodule]]). Thus the maximal proper submodule occurring
here is the sum of *all* proper graded submodules, not an arbitrarily chosen
maximal one; no choice is used.

If the pairing separates $P$, then every submodule of $M(\lambda)$ is graded,
$N(\lambda)$ is the unique maximal proper submodule, and $L(\lambda)$ is the
ordinary simple (not only graded-simple) quotient: this is the usual simple
weight-module quotient of the Verma module over a separating torus
(Verification, step 4.1).

The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`
identifies $N(\lambda)$ with the radical of the normalized Verma contravariant
form and gives the canonical normalized form on $L(\lambda)$; for $\lambda$
dominant integral, the existence theorem
`thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique` proves the
ordinary simplicity and the universal integrable conclusions. Both are
declared obligations of those later items, not assumptions here.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Throughout this pair the **source parameter** of the Fock-space literature is
written $s$ and the **library parameter** of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is written $t$; the
dictionary below sets $t=s^{-1}$.

Let $I$ be a nonempty consecutive set of simple-root indices and put $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, the coordinate alphabet. On a finite coordinate interval $J=[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ the roots have indices $[k,r-1]$, the coordinate weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a=k}^r\mathbb Z\delta_a$, $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$ and $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$. The full central coordinate is retained. The source algebra $U_s$ has toral generators $D_a^{\pm1}$ for $a\in J$ and root generators $E_a,F_a$ for $k\le a<r$, acting on natural vectors $v_b$, $b\in J$, by

$$D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b,\qquad E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}\,v_a,\qquad F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}\,v_{a+1},$$

$$\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1},\qquad \Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a .$$

The library parameter $t$ is identified with $s^{-1}$; the **semilinear Hopf
dictionary** is the coefficient map $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ together with the
generator assignment

$$E_a\longmapsto E_a,\qquad F_a\longmapsto F_a,\qquad K_h\longmapsto D_{-h},$$

where the $E_a,F_a$ on the source side are the *divided* generators of the
source normalization and on the library side those of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] (the assignments agree on the
undivided generators $E_a=E_a^{(1)}$, $F_a=F_a^{(1)}$, and divided powers are
carried to divided powers because the quantum integers are invariant under
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
Root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the
reciprocal parameter: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the library generator
$K_h$ acts by $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which is the action of $D_{-h}$ because
$(-h)(\mu)=-\mu(h)$.

The **bar involution** sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E_a$ and $F_a$ and
inverts each $D_a$; the corresponding library operation is the involution with
$t\mapsto t^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$ and
$K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]
and [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].

The **natural highest weight** attached to an interval $[k,r]$ is
$\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ (equivalently the highest weight reached by the
leading coordinate vector $v_k$), its **dual highest weight** is
$-\delta_r$, and the **fundamental wedge weight** is
$\delta_k+\delta_{k+1}+\cdots+\delta_m$ for $k\le m\le r$. Every fundamental
factor carries its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and
divided-string crystal charts ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]);
its internal antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive and integral but is *not*
asserted to be based in the library's raw lower $q_0$ chart. Infinite intervals
are defined by the compatible system of their finite subintervals, and
[[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] with
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] supplies
the library integrable modules used on each finite interval.

The source Fock families $L,T,P$ and the library form-dual upper family
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]) will
be compared below through their actual forms; they are never identified by
their names.

derivations.claim: **The normalized highest inclusion.** The explicitly constructed fundamental factors make the ground tensor integrable and give it the unique top weight $\Lambda$. The universal highest-module map from the actual existence-and-uniqueness theorem sends the normalized highest vector to this ground tensor and has nonzero image. Ordinary simplicity of that highest module makes the map $j:V(\Lambda)\to F(\Lambda)$ injective. A module injection preserves each highest kernel and the unique divided-string decomposition, hence commutes with the intrinsic lower string shifts. It also sends divided-power generators to the actual integral tensor lattice. The normalized projection will be constructed by the finite nondegenerate pairing below, rather than assumed from a general semisimplicity assertion. Its uniqueness follows from the one-dimensional top weight: a nonzero map to the simple highest module is surjective, hence cannot vanish on the top weight.

**The actual balanced tensor chart.** Let $L_0^{\rm ten}$ and $\Psi L_0^{\rm ten}$ be the actual two charts of the finite-product theorem, not the raw tensor-word chart. The normalized ground tensor is a nonzero ground crystal residue. Every generator of $L_0(\Lambda)$ is a divided-string word on its highest vector; the naturality established in step 1.1 and the actual tensor crystal rule put its image in $L_0^{\rm ten}$ with the corresponding nonzero ground-component residue, with nonvanishing ensured by the partial-inverse rule. Divided-power generation gives $jV_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)\subseteq F_{\mathcal A}$. Both bar composites agree on the highest vector and on every bar-fixed divided lowering monomial, so $j\overline{L_0(\Lambda)}\subseteq\Psi L_0^{\rm ten}$. Hence $jG(b)$ is integral, lies in both actual charts, is bar fixed and has the required residue. Balanced uniqueness identifies it with the corrected tensor global vector. Since $t=s^{-1}$, this library zero chart is the source infinity chart: the original factor order yields $T_A$ on $\mathrm{Rev}$, and the reverse-factor order yields $\widetilde T_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$. This proves based inclusion rather than assuming every module map is based.

**The ground components.** On a strict column the crystal signature rule has $+$ for entry $i$ and $-$ for entry $i+1$ with simultaneous occurrences cancelling; concatenating down-column words, cancelling $-+$ pairs, the rightmost surviving $+$ and leftmost surviving $-$ determine the source upper operators. Semistandard rows are stable under this rule: a changed entry violating a row inequality has an equal neighbouring entry which is either a later surviving $+$, an earlier surviving $-$ or its cancelling mate, and column strictness forces the last matching in the same row strip. The only highest tableau of the closed set is the ground state: the rightmost column is consecutive ground, and inducting to the left, rows overlapping the already-ground right columns are forced to be ground while a gap above the overlap produces an unmatched minus; repeated raising decreases the sum of entries, bounded below on a finite interval. Thus the reverse-factor lower ground component, equivalently the source original-order upper signature component, is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; the original-order lower component is the reverse-standard set from step 2.1.

**Rectification.** Reversing the tensor order gives the reverse reading of the same signature rule; aligning column tops by the prescribed vertical shifts makes the reverse-standard inequalities stable, and the explicit row-insertion rectification (bumping the smallest larger letter, with the elementary Knuth interchanges preserving the cancelling signs) is a weight-preserving crystal isomorphism between the original lower ground component and the reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with inverse reverse insertion. This is the label dictionary of [F1].

**The projection.** Define $\pi$ by $C_0(v,\pi y)=C(j_{\mathrm{reverse}}v,y)$, where $j_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ is the based reverse-factor highest inclusion. The required highest form is constructed from the actual library polarization $B_8$: at weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ put $C_0=s^{a(\alpha)}B_8$, $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$. Its nondegeneracy and highest value one follow from $B_8$. The translated adjoint is $\sigma(F_i)=sK_i^{-1}E_i$, $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. For input weight $\mu$ this contributes $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$, canceled by $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Thus $C_0(F_ix,y)=C_0(x,E_i y)$, and similarly $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_i y)$; toral operators remain self-adjoint. This constructs, rather than assumes, the normalized nondegenerate $\mathcal E\mathcal F$-contravariant form. Here is the needed typed contravariance locally. Let $B_0$ be the coefficient dot pairing of reversed and original tensor words, and write $\Psi=\Theta\overline{(\cdot)}_0$ on a finite product, with $\overline{(\cdot)}_0$ the factorwise coefficient bar. Since $\Psi M_B=\Theta M_B$, the normalization $C(\widetilde M_A,\Psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}$ gives $C(x,y)=B_0(x,\Theta^{-1}y)$. On each minuscule factor the matrices of $E_i$ and $F_i$ are transposes. Reversing the factors in the explicit coproduct therefore gives $B_0(E_i x,z)=B_0(x,\overline\Delta(F_i)z)$, $B_0(F_i x,z)=B_0(x,\overline\Delta(E_i)z)$, while toral $D_a$ is self-adjoint. The finite quasi-$R$ intertwiner satisfies $\Theta\overline\Delta(u)=\Delta(\overline u)\Theta$; for $E_i,F_i$ their bars equal themselves. Substitution proves $C(E_i x,y)=C(x,F_i y)$, $C(F_i x,y)=C(x,E_i y)$ and $C(D_a x,y)=C(x,D_a y)$, first on two factors and then by coproduct association on each finite product. The required complementary delta pairing can also be checked here. The paired-root Casimir terms of the finite quasi-$R$ expansion, under factor reversal and the minuscule $E/F$ transpose, give $\Theta_{\mathrm{reverse}}^{\mathsf T}=\overline\Theta^{-1}$; the inverse/factorization identities extend this from two factors to every finite product. Consequently $C$ commutes with both bars in the sense $C(\widetilde\Psi x,\Psi y)=\overline{C(x,y)}$. Since $L_B=\Theta\overline{L_B}_0$, one has $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=B_0(\widetilde T_A,\overline{L_B}_0)$. The two coefficient families on the right have coefficients in $\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$, with constant matrix the identity and every off-diagonal term in $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$. Their value is bar fixed by the preceding identity, hence belongs to $\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\cap\mathbb Z[s]=\mathbb Z$, forcing $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$. The triangular bar-fixed families used here are obtained locally in finite weight spaces: at each lower label, involutivity makes the residual coefficient $r(s)$ satisfy $r(s)+r(s^{-1})=0$; its positive-power part, or negative-power part, gives the unique required correction, and induction on the finite lower ideal constructs the complementary charts. Thus this use requires neither an unproved Gram identity nor a presumed based embedding. These identities are over $\mathbb Q(s)$; any stated complex coefficient conjugation is restored on scalar extension. Thus the normalized highest form $C_0$ has precisely the required $E/F$ adjunction and toral symmetry, and $\pi$ is $U$-linear; its highest coefficient is $1$, so its composite with the original highest inclusion is the identity on the simple highest module. It is therefore a genuine normalized projection, and its uniqueness is the top-weight argument of step 1.1.

**Vanishing and the dual-canonical basis.** Since $j_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ sends the lower global basis to $\widetilde T_A$ with $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, the delta pairing $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [F1] gives $\pi L_B=0$ for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, while for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the vectors $D_A=\pi L_A$ form the $C_0$-dual basis of the constituent. This proves the vanishing statement (2) and that the $D_A$ are the source dual-canonical basis.

**Straightening and the $S$-basis.** Expanding $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ by the triangular chart of [F1] and applying $\pi$ gives $\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$ the restriction to $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ of a unitriangular matrix with diagonal $1$; hence the projected monomials $S_A=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of the constituent and the displayed formula is the explicit straightening of every projected monomial, standard or not. No projected-monomial vanishing is claimed.

**The integral kernel and the source upper lattice.** By step 6.1 the kernel of $\pi$ is spanned by the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; being spanned by a subset of a basis it is a saturated direct summand of the integral Fock lattice. The image $\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ is spanned by the $D_A$, hence is the source upper/costandard lattice; it is not identified with the lower divided-power lattice by an $A$-unit Gram determinant, since the relevant monomial Gram matrices are the inverse ordinary-bar matrix rather than the identity.

**Cuts and the direct limit.** All constructions and all coefficients of steps 1.1-8.1 are stable under the upper-cut and common-tail embeddings by the declared truncation compatibility theorem, and every vector lies in some finite double cut; the normalized highest maps are unique, so the maps agree on overlaps. The compatible direct limit gives the full bounded or semi-infinite assertion, and the comparison with the library form-dual upper family is the explicit weight rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison.

**Conclusion.** The highest Fock constituent $V(\Lambda)$ has the standard monomial basis $S_A$ and the source dual-canonical basis $D_A=[\pi L_A]$ over $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with the explicit straightening formula and the saturated integral kernel off $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; the library comparison uses the weight rescaling only.

derivations.claim: **Definition of the functors.** Tensoring with $V$ or $V^{*}$ preserves $\mathcal O$ and parabolic local finiteness: tensor a finite parabolic span of a vector with the finite tensor factor. Exact central-character projection therefore defines the stated functors. Replacing $i$ by $i+1$ changes the Fock weight by $-\alpha_i$, so a source weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ becomes $\Lambda-(\alpha+\alpha_i)$; the reverse move gives $\alpha-\alpha_i$. A target with no admitted tableau is the zero category and its projection is zero.

**Exactness and biadjunction.** On the direct sum of blocks, exactness is inherited from the exactness of tensoring with a finite-dimensional module and of the block projections [F1]. Biadjunction holds because the general clause of the published translation supplier applies to the finite modules $V$ and $V^{*}$ without any regular-wall crossing: the unit and counit are those of the tensor/block-projection adjunction, and they restrict to the stated blocks by construction of the projections.

**The Casimir description.** The well-definedness supplier [F6] computes the tensor-Casimir scalars on generalized-standard flag sections: a valid $\lambda\mapsto\lambda+\varepsilon_j$ section has scalar $a_j$, and a valid $\lambda\mapsto\lambda-\varepsilon_j$ section has scalar $-a_j-n+1$. In particular the reverse move from entry $i+1$ has scalar $-n-i$. Its extension from these flag sections to arbitrary finite-length objects proves that the generalized $i$-eigencomponent is $f_i$ and the generalized $-n-i$-eigencomponent is $e_i$, with the block shifts of step 1.1.

**Projectives and injectives.** The biadjunction of step 2.1 holds inside the parabolic blocks. For a projective $P$, the identity $\operatorname{Hom}(f_iP,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_i-)$ is exact because $e_i$ is exact, so $f_iP$ is projective; interchange the functors for the other direction. For an injective $J$, $\operatorname{Hom}(-,f_iJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(e_i-,J)$ is exact, and again interchange the functors. Thus both preserve projectives and injectives in the stated categories.

**Commutation with duality.** Restricted transpose duality fixes $V$ and $V^{*}$ with their respective forms and commutes with tensoring with a fixed finite-dimensional module and with the character projections; therefore $D f_i\cong f_i D$ and $D e_i\cong e_i D$ on the direct sum, which is the stated compatibility.

**Conclusion.** The residue translation functors $f_i,e_i$ on the direct sum of finite classical blocks are exact, biadjoint, preserve projectives and injectives, commute with restricted duality, and agree with the stated Casimir eigencomponents; they are special residue translations with the Fock root label shifts, not ordinary regular-wall translations and not classical highest-weight shifts.

derivations.claim: **The degenerate affine Hecke relations.** Write $x=\sum_{a,b}E_{ab}\otimes E_{ba}$ and let $x_j$ include the place swaps with the preceding $j-1$ natural factors. Direct matrix-unit multiplication in the natural module gives $T_j^2=1$, the braid relation for adjacent places, commutation of distant places, and $T_jx_jT_j=x_{j+1}-T_j$, which is equivalent to $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$; the Casimir components and the place operators commute as required. Hence the listed relations hold on $M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$.

**The Casimir scalars on flag sections.** Write $C=\sum_{a,b}E_{ab}E_{ba}$. The matrix-unit brackets show that $C$ is central and that its highest-weight scalar is $c(\lambda)=\sum_j\lambda_j(\lambda_j+n+1-2j)$: commute each positive root factor past its negative partner and apply it to the highest vector. Moreover $\Delta(C)=C\otimes1+1\otimes C+2x$ and $c(V)=c(V^{*})=n$. On a valid generalized-standard section of highest weight $\lambda+\varepsilon_j$, $x$ therefore has scalar $(c(\lambda+\varepsilon_j)-c(\lambda)-n)/2=\lambda_j+1-j=a_j$; the section $\lambda-\varepsilon_j$ has scalar $-a_j-n+1$. Thus $i\to i+1$ selects scalar $i$, and $i+1\to i$ selects scalar $-n-i$. The generalized-standard tensor flags will be constructed below; these formulas concern their sections and do not assert scalar action on arbitrary weight vectors.

**The operator relations and dual mates.** The operators $x_j,T_j$ are natural endomorphisms of the tensor functors, so the relations of step 1.1 restrict to simultaneous generalized residue components whenever those components are defined. Taking mates under the tensor/block biadjunction transfers the operator identities to the reverse functors, with the dual-Casimir shift $-n-i$ of step 1.2. The nilpotence and identification of these components with block projections are verified after constructing the flags.

**Multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags.** Filter $V|_{\mathfrak p}$ by its successive Levi blocks and $V^{*}|_{\mathfrak p}$ by the reverse blocks; each section is a natural or dual natural Levi module with radical acting by zero. For a finite Levi simple $E(\lambda)$, the Weyl numerator identity $A(\lambda+\rho_{\mathfrak l})\sum_j e^{\varepsilon_j}=\sum_j A(\lambda+\rho_{\mathfrak l}+\varepsilon_j)$ gives $E(\lambda)\otimes V_b=\bigoplus_jE(\lambda+\varepsilon_j)$ over the dominant valid moves in block $b$: an invalid move makes two shifted coordinates equal and its alternating numerator zero. The same identity with $-\varepsilon_j$ treats the dual. Levi complete reducibility, part of the parabolic structure [F3], turns these character identities into multiplicity-one decompositions. The tensor identity for induction maps $u\otimes(e\otimes v)$ to $\sum(u_{(1)}\otimes e)\otimes u_{(2)}v$, with inverse given by the antipode; the coproduct/antipode identities verify balancing and inverse composition. PBW makes induction exact, so the resulting filtration of $\Delta(A)\otimes V$ or $\Delta(A)\otimes V^{*}$ has precisely the generalized-standard sections for these valid moves. Their central characters are the changed entry multisets, and step 1.2 gives the Casimir scalar on each section. Exact block or generalized-eigenspace projection therefore retains precisely the specified moves, each once.

**Eigencomponents on all objects.** Projectives have finite standard flags, and tensoring their flags with either finite factor gives the flags of step 2.2. On a chosen block component the Casimir differs from its indicated scalar by an operator zero on every flag section, so a power bounded by the flag length annihilates that component. Distinct scalars give distinct changed multisets. Every finite-length object is a quotient of a finite sum of these projectives; naturality of $x$ and exactness of both projections extend the block/eigencomponent identification and nilpotence to all objects. Apply this successively to each tensor place to obtain the natural affine-Hecke action on repeated residue functors, with each $x_j-i$ locally nilpotent.

**The integral Fock $K_0$ action.** The standard classes form a basis in each block by [F3], and the monomials of [F4] have exactly those labels, so $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Step 2.2 identifies the induced operators with the tensor/wedge operators at $s=1$; their Chevalley/Serre relations follow from the Fock module. On a tensor of minuscule wedges, $f_i^r$ counts ordered choices of $r$ distinct movable columns; every subset occurs $r!$ times, and the same holds for $e_i^r$. Thus the divided class operators are integral as well. Each residue operator is nilpotent on any fixed weight calculation by the finite-cut Fock action; positivity in the simple basis and finite length then imply the corresponding iterated functor vanishes. The locally finite $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action follows. The ground-state class generates its highest constituent; the other standard classes supply the rest of the tensor Fock module.

**Conclusion.** The tensor Casimir and place swaps give the degenerate affine Hecke relations on the finite classical tensor products, restrict to the residue functors with local nilpotence and biadjoint mates, produce multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags, and induce the integral Fock $K_0$ action with Chevalley/Serre relations, local integrability and positivity.

At the coincident eigenvalue, $x_i-x_{i+1}+1$ is a unit, so $\partial_i=(x_i-x_{i+1}+1)^{-1}(1-T_i)$ with the inverse on the left; hence the completed algebra is the polynomial/divided-difference endomorphism algebra $\mathrm{End}_{P_r^{S_r}}(P_r)$.

The Nullstellensatz makes $Z_{i,r}$ finite; it is a homogeneous system of parameters in the weighted polynomial ring, which is Cohen-Macaulay, so [F2] supplies regularity; the Koszul Euler series gives $\dim Z_{i,r}=\prod_{j=r-i+1}^{r}j/\prod_{j=1}^{i}j=\binom{r}{i}$, and the two-Koszul socle computation gives a unique socle in degree $i(r-i)$, hence a local Frobenius ring.
