These are finite by [F1]; at weight $\lambda$, ordinary $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ string theory gives $d(b)=2h_+(b)+\lambda+1=2h_-(b)-\lambda+1$. Positivity implies that every simple constituent $c$ of $eb$ has $h_+(c)\le h_+(b)-1$, so $d(c)\le d(b)$; the $f$ argument is identical. Hence the Serre subcategory generated by simples with $d\le r$ is stable under $E,F$. If $T$ is a simple subobject of $E^jM$, adjunction gives a nonzero map $F^jT\to M$; its image contains a simple subobject $S$ of $M$, and the preceding bound gives $d(S)\le d(T)$. The dual argument applies to simple quotients. Consequently translates of an object of height at most $r$ whose simple head and socle constituents all have height $r$ have the same property.

Since both matrices are unitriangular, their inverses identify the simple class $[L(A)]$ with the actual source vector $L_A$ at $1$. The standard-class translation action of [F1] therefore carries this simple-class identification through every residue iteration.

The completed fibre is therefore $\mathrm{Mat}_{r!}(\mathbb C)$, with its unique simple module of dimension $r!$.

classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ category $\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
distinct from the Fock algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$.

Let $x_j$ be the tensor Casimir acting on the $j$-th natural factor of
$M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ together with all preceding factors, and let $T_j$ be
the adjacent place swap. Then the **degenerate affine Hecke relations** hold:
the $x_j$ commute, the $T_j$ satisfy the symmetric-group braid and quadratic
relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$, and distant generators commute. They restrict
naturally to the repeated residue functors $f_i^r$ of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]], where
$x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; the dual actions are the biadjoint mates on
$e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give
multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock
$K_0$ action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's
biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class
generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $I$ bounded below use
the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
including repeated entries. Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let
$w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young
stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,\,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the **antispherical/sign** family for the entry stabilizer, in the left
convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library quantum
parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal $1$, and
$d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The **column Levi**
subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. The genuine parabolic block
composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,\,d(A)w_0}(1),$$

**spherical** coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi
cancellation, so it covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does
not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic $\mathcal O$ and does
not identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.

so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$

[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central

([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. ([[def-abelian-category]]). Its set of isomorphism classes is denoted

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The standard-class map is an isomorphism.** In each finite block the standard classes form a basis of the Grothendieck group and characters are injective, while the residue functors act on the standard basis by the explicit single-entry moves; the Fock monomials satisfy the identical relations and have the same degrees. Hence $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ is a degree-preserving isomorphism in each block, and it extends to the direct sum over the blocks because the direct sum decomposition is by central character on both sides.

**The transition matrix and duality at $1$.** Write $D_{A,B}=d_{A,B}(1)=[M(B):L(A)]$ with simple rows and standard columns. Then $[M(B)]=\sum_A D_{A,B}[L(A)]$, so it is the simple-to-standard expansion that uses $D^{-1}$. BGG reciprocity instead gives $[P(A):M(B)]=D_{A,B}$, hence $[P(A)]=\sum_BD_{A,B}[M(B)]$; this matrix is the transposed standard/simple multiplicity array when rows are projective labels, not its inverse. Under the standard-class map these are exactly the defining $P_A$ and $L_A$ expansions. On the actual finite type-$A$ cuts, each nonconstant term of the quasi-$R$ root-factor expansion has a factor $s-s^{-1}$ and coefficients regular at $s=1$ (the quantum-factorial denominators have nonzero ordinary-factorial values there). Thus the tensor bar matrix specializes to the identity; passage to the primitive wedge factors preserves this specialization. The source monomial Gram matrices, which are its inverse, are consequently the identity at $1$. Multiplying the $D$ projective array by the $D^{-1}$ simple array yields $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$. No inverse BGG multiplicity matrix is asserted.

**The general Hom pairing.** For a projective $P$ and a finite-length $N$, the functor $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ is exact, so its dimension on $N$ is additive on a composition series and equals the pairing of $[P]$ with $[N]$ under the $P/L$ duality of step 2.1; in particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$. This is a projective/simple statement: the standard/simple matrix is the unitriangular mixed multiplicity matrix, not the identity, so no standard/simple orthogonality is claimed.

**Conclusion.** The standard-class map identifies the direct-sum $K_0$ with the integral Fock module compatibly with degrees and the residue Chevalley action; the projective/simple pairing is the Fock pairing at $s=1$, giving $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, while standard/simple orthogonality is false; the projective, simple and tilting bases are proved separately.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1: the zero class and the empty direct sum lie in the identified Grothendieck group.
Step 2.1: the specialization s=1 makes the off-diagonal pairing entries vanish on the simple/projective delta.
Step 1.1: the diagonal standard classes and the unitriangular transition are the one-step case of the isomorphism.
Step 1.1: matching multiset degrees cover repeated entries and singular characters.
Step 1.1: the degrees of the ground and top classes are the endpoints of the degree-preserving isomorphism.
The Statement assumes AC; standard bases and projective covers via [F2] and [F5] use it.
Step 2.1: ⟨P_A,L_B⟩=δ_{AB} from the duality of the transition matrices, the forward direction.
Step 2.1: unitriangular inversion gives the equality of the pairing with the Fock form in both directions.

risk_review.notes: All four steps and18 direct supplier statements reviewed. Simple/standard bases, direct-sum finite support, degree matching and standard-class Chevalley action follow independently from finite highest-weight and Casimir suppliers. BGG uses composition rows A, standard columns B: projective coefficients D_(A,B), simple expansion D^-1, never inverse BGG. Finite-Cartan quasi-R nonconstant coefficients vanish at s=1 with regular factorial denominators, so monomial Gram specializes to I. Exact projective Hom adds along composition series. However the actual categorical D=d(1), and consequently the general Hom/Fock pairing under standard-class identification in Proof2.1–3.1, still require the escalated KL coefficient bridge. citations.quote:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

(3) All bases and maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings, so
the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight
rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison, not an unqualified
identification.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

Throughout this pair the **source parameter** of the Fock-space literature is
written $s$ and the **library parameter** of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] is written $t$; the
dictionary below sets $t=s^{-1}$.

Let $I$ be a nonempty consecutive set of simple-root indices and put $I^+=I\cup(I+1)$, the coordinate alphabet. On a finite coordinate interval $J=[k,r]\subseteq I^+$ the roots have indices $[k,r-1]$, the coordinate weight lattice is $\bigoplus_{a=k}^r\mathbb Z\delta_a$, $\alpha_a=\delta_a-\delta_{a+1}$ and $h_a=e_a-e_{a+1}$. The full central coordinate is retained. The source algebra $U_s$ has toral generators $D_a^{\pm1}$ for $a\in J$ and root generators $E_a,F_a$ for $k\le a<r$, acting on natural vectors $v_b$, $b\in J$, by

$$D_av_b=s^{\delta_{ab}}v_b,\qquad E_av_b=\delta_{a+1,b}\,v_a,\qquad F_av_b=\delta_{a,b}\,v_{a+1},$$

$$\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1},\qquad \Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a .$$

The library parameter $t$ is identified with $s^{-1}$; the **semilinear Hopf
dictionary** is the coefficient map $t\mapsto s^{-1}$ together with the
generator assignment

$$E_a\longmapsto E_a,\qquad F_a\longmapsto F_a,\qquad K_h\longmapsto D_{-h},$$

where the $E_a,F_a$ on the source side are the *divided* generators of the
source normalization and on the library side those of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] (the assignments agree on the
undivided generators $E_a=E_a^{(1)}$, $F_a=F_a^{(1)}$, and divided powers are
carried to divided powers because the quantum integers are invariant under
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).
Root-label weights are preserved, while toral numerical eigenvalues use the
reciprocal parameter: on a weight vector of weight $\mu$ the library generator
$K_h$ acts by $t^{\mu(h)}=s^{-\mu(h)}$, which is the action of $D_{-h}$ because
$(-h)(\mu)=-\mu(h)$.

The **bar involution** sends $s\mapsto s^{-1}$, fixes $E_a$ and $F_a$ and
inverts each $D_a$; the corresponding library operation is the involution with
$t\mapsto t^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$ and
$K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]
and [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].

The **natural highest weight** attached to an interval $[k,r]$ is
$\delta_k=\varepsilon_k$ (equivalently the highest weight reached by the
leading coordinate vector $v_k$), its **dual highest weight** is
$-\delta_r$, and the **fundamental wedge weight** is
$\delta_k+\delta_{k+1}+\cdots+\delta_m$ for $k\le m\le r$. Every fundamental
factor carries its own highest-vector-normalized bar, integral lattice and
divided-string crystal charts ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]);
its internal antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive and integral but is *not*
asserted to be based in the library's raw lower $q_0$ chart. Infinite intervals
are defined by the compatible system of their finite subintervals, and
[[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]] with
[[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]] supplies
the library integrable modules used on each finite interval.

The source Fock families $L,T,P$ and the library form-dual upper family
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]) will
be compared below through their actual forms; they are never identified by
their names.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

For any finite sequence of based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space category $O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the field tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\text{composite factor bars})$, built from the normalized intertwiner $\Theta$ of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], is well defined, semilinear, $U$- and bar-compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations; all root-height sums are vectorwise finite.

This field assertion holds for arbitrary based pairs and does not imply integral action. Its integral and based assertion holds for exactly the admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]: highest-first or first $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest or $C_{\mathrm{low}}$ second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients and direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs and products in finite Cartan type. For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently proved integral $\Theta$ action, not on field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.

In these cases: $\Psi$ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice; its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal $1$; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors modulo $q$, with corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; they form a genuine $A$-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple; the $q=0$ tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], and the infinity chart is $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$, not an asserted bar containment in $L_0$, since semilinearity sends $q$ to $q^{-1}$. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. Exact based integral and bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-$R$ braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action; the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter.

**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module that is integrable, has finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight set contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).

(i) **Splitting along the top isotypic part.** Let $\lambda$ be a maximal weight of $M$, put $N_0:=U_q(\mathfrak g)M_\lambda$ and let $N_1$ be the sum of the remaining simple constituents, so that $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$. Then $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$, $B=\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_0)/q(L\cap N_0)\bigr)\sqcup\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_1)/q(L\cap N_1)\bigr)$, and both pairs are crystal bases of $N_0$ and $N_1$.

(ii) **Uniqueness.** There is a locally weight-finite indexed family $(\lambda_j)_{j\in J}$ in $P^+$ and an isomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules $\Phi:M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{j\in J}V(\lambda_j)$ with $\Phi(L)=\bigoplus_j\mathcal L(\lambda_j)$ and $\Phi$ inducing a bijection $B\to\bigsqcup_j\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ of crystals. The multiset $\{\lambda_j:j\in J\}$ is the multiset of highest weights of the simple integrable constituents of $M$: the number of $j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda$ equals the multiplicity $[M:V(\lambda)]$.

(iii) **Components.** Through $\Phi$ the connected components of the crystal $B$ are exactly the canonical highest weight crystals $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$; each component has a unique highest weight element $b$, of dominant weight $\lambda$, and equals the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]. In particular the crystal graph of any crystal basis of $M$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$, and no other highest weight elements occur.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and used to obtain the decomposition of $M$ into simple integrable highest weight modules from [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], which selects a maximal independent family of simple submodules simultaneously. It also permits simultaneous choices of lifts of the finite residue bases in the possibly infinite family of top spaces. After those choices, each lattice and crystal argument is finite and choice-free. No incompatible-axiom branch is used, and no global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness is assumed. The index set $J$ need not be finite in affine or indefinite type; local weight finiteness means only finitely many summands contribute to any fixed label-weight space.

derivations.claim: **The lower family and the pairing.** By [F1] the based highest inclusion identifies the corrected tensor family $T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ with the lower global basis on $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and the projection $\pi$ is its $C_0$-adjoint; hence $C_0(T_{A^{\uparrow}},D_B)=\delta_{AB}$.

**The weight recursion $B_8=s^{-a}C_0$.** The generator identities of the dictionary determine the library contravariant form $B_8$ and the normalized source form $C_0$ compatibly; on weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ the semilinear normalization gives $B_8=s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$. Indeed the dictionary sends the library $\sigma$ at $t=s^{-1}$ to the source anti-involution, whose action on a lowered vector of weight $\mu$ contributes $s^{-\langle\mu,h_i\rangle-1}$, and the exponent identity $a(\alpha)-a(\alpha-\alpha_i)=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+1$ with highest normalization and induction on lowering monomials proves the equality on every weight space.

**Identification of the upper family.** Applying step 1.2 to step 1.1 gives $B_8(T_{A^{\uparrow}},s^{a}D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; by the dual-family uniqueness in [F2], the vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$ are the actual library form-dual upper vectors, fixed by the form-adjoint upper bar with the genuine dual lattices and charts.

**The quasi-canonical family on the constituent.** The source form satisfies $\langle x,y\rangle=s^{a}C_0(\psi x,y)$ on the constituent. To verify the actual recurrence, put $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. The coefficient Gram formula $\Theta^{-1}$ and the minuscule generator transpose identities give $\langle E_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,sF_iK_i^{-1}y\rangle$, $\langle F_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,s^{-1}K_iE_i y\rangle$ and the toral adjoint $D_a^{-1}$; the finite coproduct intertwiner transports these identities through each tensor prefix. For example, on input weight $\mu$ the first adjoint has scalar $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$. This is precisely the ratio $s^{a(\alpha)-a(\alpha+\alpha_i)}$, since $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Together with $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_iy)$, the ordinary bar and highest value one, induction on divided lowering monomials proves the displayed identity. These comparisons are made over $\mathbb Q(s)$, with the specified coefficient conjugation on complex scalar extension. The left annihilator of $\ker\pi$ under this form is $U$-stable by its anti-involution, contains the ground highest vector, and has dimension $\dim V(\Lambda)$; hence it is exactly the highest constituent. The delta evaluations of the quasi-canonical vectors show that $P_A$ lies in that annihilator for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; on the constituent the candidate $s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ has the same delta evaluations against the $D$-basis by step 1.2 and annihilates the off-standard $L$-vectors by [F1], so whole-Fock dual uniqueness gives $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on $V(\Lambda)$.

**Integrality, cuts and limits.** The units $s^{\pm a(\alpha)}$ are Laurent monomials, so the $D$-to-library-upper and $P$-to-library-lower comparisons of steps 1.1-3.1 are separately weightwise integral; their charts are the corresponding actual rescaled or dual charts. This is not a comparison of the embedded upper and lower lattices with each other. The finite double-cut compatibility of the Fock bases and of the library global bases, together with uniqueness of the normalized highest maps, proves the full direct-limit statement, and only the actual integral and specialization clauses of [F4] are used.

**Conclusion.** The library lower global vector is $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=s^{-a}P_A$, the actual form-dual upper vector is $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$, and the source quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on the highest constituent; the source $D$ image lattice compares with the library form-dual upper lattice by $s^a$, while the source $P$ lattice compares with the library lower divided-power lattice by $s^{-a}$; the embedded upper and lower lattices are kept distinct, and no ordinary-bar fixedness is claimed for the unqualified library upper family.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
$$\Phi(\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(E))\cong\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*).$$
The parabolic in this formula is unchanged.

(4) Let $c(X)=-w_0X^{\mathsf T}w_0$, which carries the upper Borel to itself and reverses the Levi blocks, and set $\Psi=c^*\Phi$. For a lower-bounded tableau shape set $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and use the concatenated ordinary highest-weight reading $a_i$, with each column read from top to bottom in strictly decreasing order, and $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$. The source reading is the reversed sequence of columns, without reversing positions within a column. Then
$$\Psi:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A).$$
This is an exact contravariant equivalence. It preserves the tableau label and the corresponding central-character summands, including the scalar central coordinate, and the reverse-column label order is opposite to the target order. More explicitly its weight map is
$$\lambda\longmapsto w_0w_{\bar J}\lambda+2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}.$$

(5) For restricted BGG transpose duality $D$, the composite $F=D\Psi$ is an exact covariant equivalence $\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$ with $F(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\nabla(A)$.

For category-$\mathcal O$ modules these constructions use finite weight spaces and the finite direct sum of $\zeta$-eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Internal homogeneous Hom becomes the $\zeta$-locally finite part of Hom, and the dual is the weight-restricted dual. No equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or unrestricted completed Hom spaces is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published category-$\mathcal O$ theory. Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard
parabolic of
[[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with
reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$, nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$ and Weyl
group $W_J$; the ambient category is $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]
with standard objects the Verma modules [[def-verma-module]].

**(1) Dominance for the Levi.** A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant**
if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all
$\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular
$\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$; see
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]] for the ambient
notion).

**(2) Generalized Verma modules.** For a $\mathfrak p$-dominant $\lambda$ let
$E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained
from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight
$\lambda$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero. Define the **generalized Verma module**

$$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$

**(3) The parabolic category.** The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely
generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which
$U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely, that is, on which every vector lies
in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule; equivalently, every vector
lies in a finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak l_J$-submodule and is annihilated by a power of $\mathfrak u_J$
(local finiteness for the nilpotent $\mathfrak u_J$).

The following structural facts are part of the definition; the arguments are
given in the Remarks.

**(4) Generalized Vermas lie in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.** For each
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$, $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is an
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ with highest weight $\lambda$, and the
natural surjection $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$
exhibits $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ as the largest quotient of the Verma
module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(5) Simples.** The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly
the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral
([[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]).

**(6) Serre property.** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects,
quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$; in particular it is an abelian
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ stable under finite direct sums.

**(7) Costandard objects.** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ put
$\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, the restricted
dual of [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]].
These are the **costandard objects** of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; each is
naturally a submodule of the ordinary dual Verma $D M(\lambda)$. They need not
be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every projective object
of $\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

More precisely, each projective cover $P(\mu)$ produced by
[[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]] is a direct summand of the
projective object $\operatorname{pr}_C(E\otimes M(\lambda))$ of
[[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]], which is a
direct summand of $E\otimes M(\lambda)$; a general projective object has
finite length, hence is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives,
each of which is a projective cover of its simple head.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every weight
$\lambda$ the restricted dual $I(\lambda)=D(P(\lambda))$ of the projective
cover is an injective object of $\mathcal O$
([[def-injective-object]]) and has a finite costandard ($\nabla$-)flag, with
multiplicities
$$(I(\lambda):\nabla(\mu))=(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]$$
in the sense of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
[[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]; the functor $D$ exchanges Verma flags of projectives
with costandard flags of injectives. Every injective object of $\mathcal O$
has a finite costandard flag: it is a finite direct sum of indecomposable
injectives, and $D$ induces a bijection between the indecomposable projectives
and the indecomposable injectives of $\mathcal O$
([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]); each
indecomposable injective is the dual of an indecomposable projective and hence
of the form $I(\lambda)$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category in which every object has finite
length, and define an object to be **indecomposable** when it is nonzero and
every decomposition $X\cong Y\oplus Z$ has $Y=0$ or $Z=0$. Then:

1. every object of $\mathcal A$ is a finite direct sum of indecomposable
   objects;
2. the endomorphism ring of an indecomposable object is local, and for an
   endomorphism $f$ of an indecomposable object either $f$ is an isomorphism
   or $f$ is nilpotent;
3. the decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and permutation of the
   summands;
4. an indecomposable projective object $P$ of $\mathcal A$ has a unique
   maximal proper subobject $J(P)$, its quotient $P/J(P)$ is simple, and $P$
   is a projective cover of $P/J(P)$
   ([[def-projective-object]], [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]];
   projectivity here is relative to $\mathcal A$. In a full subcategory closed
   under submodules, essentiality is the superfluous-kernel condition of the
   cited module definition; projectivity in the ambient module category is
   not asserted).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If a projective object
$P$ of $\mathcal O$ admits an epimorphism $P\twoheadrightarrow L$ onto a
simple object $L$, then some indecomposable direct summand of $P$ maps onto
$L$, and that summand is a projective cover of $L$ (an essential epimorphism
with projective source, [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]).
Any two projective covers of $L$ are isomorphic, although not canonically so,
and the endomorphism ring of a projective cover is local. In particular, for
every simple $L$ there is at most one isomorphism class of indecomposable
projectives with head $L$; when such a cover exists it is written $P(L)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The exact residue
functors of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] on the
genuine finite-$n$ parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free
generalized-standard flags given by the valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

(1) Their $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock
Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the
standard basis.

(2) For each simple $L(A)$, a residue translate vanishes exactly when the
corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual
indecomposable with simple equal head and socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$, respectively
$L(\tilde e_iA)$.

(3) The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the
ground-state class, with
$M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one
highest constituent.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Construction from actual exact sequences.** Let $\bar P(A)$ be the labelled opposite projective cover. Its highest-weight sequence is $0\to\bar K(A)\to\bar P(A)\to\bar\Delta(A)\to0$, with $\bar K(A)$ standard-filtered by labels strictly above $A$. Applying $\Psi$ gives $0\to M(A)\to X(A)\to\Psi\bar K(A)\to0$, where $X(A)=\Psi\bar P(A)$ and the quotient has a finite standard flag with labels strictly below $A$. Its endomorphism algebra is the opposite of the local endomorphism algebra of $\bar P(A)$, so $X(A)$ is indecomposable. For an arbitrary extension $0\to X(A)\to Z\to M(B)\to0$, extension closure makes $Z$ standard-filtered. Inverting $\Psi$ turns this into an extension with source projective $\bar P(A)$ as quotient, which splits; exact equivalence transfers the splitting back. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),X(A))=0$ for every $B$. The proved homological criterion of [F1] gives a costandard flag of $X(A)$, so it is the required actual tilting object with normalized bottom-standard inclusion.

**Uniqueness.** Let $T,T'$ be two indecomposable tilting objects with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and all other labels $\prec A$. Extending the common normalized bottom inclusion both ways uses $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ vanishing against standard flags, and the resulting composites restrict to the identity on the bottom standard, hence are not nilpotent; finite-dimensional local $\operatorname{End}$ and Fitting's lemma force them to be isomorphisms. So $T\cong T'$, and [F1] identifies its unique maximal support label as $A$.

**Every tilting is a sum of these.** Let $T\ne0$ be an arbitrary tilting object and let $\Gamma$ be the lower ideal generated by its entire composition support. Choose one maximal support label $A$, which is maximal in $\Gamma$, and put $m=[T:L(A)]\ge1$. All standard and costandard sections of $T$ have labels in $\Gamma$, so it is tilting in that truncated highest-weight category. The proved maximal-standard trace in [F1] injects $\Delta(A)^{\oplus m}$ into $T$ with standard-filtered quotient. Choose one copy $i:\Delta(A)\hookrightarrow T$; its quotient is still standard-filtered, since the other $m-1$ copies and the trace quotient have such flags. Let $j:\Delta(A)\hookrightarrow X(A)$ be the actual normalized inclusion of step 1.1. Since $X(A)/\Delta(A)$ is standard-filtered and $T$ is tilting, $\operatorname{Ext}^1(X(A)/\Delta(A),T)=0$ extends $i$ to $f:X(A)\to T$ with $fj=i$. Similarly $\operatorname{Ext}^1(T/\Delta(A),X(A))=0$ extends $j$ to $g:T\to X(A)$ with $gi=j$. The composite $gf$ fixes the nonzero bottom standard of the indecomposable $X(A)$, so it is invertible by the finite local-End/Fitting argument. Hence $f$ splits with retraction $(gf)^{-1}g$, and $T\cong X(A)\oplus T'$. The complement is tilting by summand closure and has strictly smaller length; induction proves the stated finite decomposition. Incomparable maximal support labels and multiplicities $m>1$ are both allowed: no normalized flag of the entire $T$ was assumed.

**Duality, ideals and Grothendieck basis.** Restricted duality makes $DT(A)$ an indecomposable tilting object with the same composition support $\le A$ and $[DT(A):L(A)]=1$. In the lower highest-weight ideal of labels $\le A$, the maximal-standard trace proved in [F1] gives an inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow DT(A)$ with standard-filtered quotient of strictly smaller labels, since its multiplicity space has dimension one. This supplies an actual normalized standard flag, so uniqueness identifies $DT(A)\cong T(A)$. If $\Gamma$ is a lower ideal containing $A$, every support label of $T(A)$ lies in $\Gamma$, so $T(A)$ computed in the ambient block lies in the Serre subcategory of $\Gamma$ and coincides with the partial tilting there; the classes $[T(A)]$ are unitriangular in the standard basis by the flag multiplicities, hence form a Grothendieck basis.

**The projection kernel and standard embeddings.** The projection $\pi$ of [F4] has kernel spanned by the $L$-vectors off $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and is $U$-stable; the residue functors have nonnegative composition coefficients, so iterating them on an off-standard simple never produces a standard composition factor. For this embedding argument, enlarge a finite upper alphabet if necessary while keeping the lower endpoint and the Levi column heights fixed. The blocks of the original labels are unchanged, because their entry multisets are unchanged; the established Fock projection and its off-standard kernel apply on the enlarged alphabet, where the standard predicate for those labels is the same. Every generalized standard $M(B)$ then embeds into an iterated $e$-word applied to an irreducible standard $M(C)$: add successively huge offsets to the later columns so that all later entries lie above the earlier ones, making $C$ the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order and hence $M(C)=L(C)$ simple; then lower the later-column entries back, column by column and bottom to top, with the explicit residue word. A later column stays above the active residues, so a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight; hence $B$ is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once, and the canonical maximal trace embeds $M(B)$ at the bottom. If $L(A)$ embedded into $M(B)$ with $A$ off standard, adjunction would give the standard $L(C)$ as a quotient of an $f$-word applied to $L(A)$, impossible by kernel stability.

**Converse and prinjectivity.** Conversely every standard label is reached from the ground simple projective by the crystal $f$-word, and the simple-head clause of [F4] makes $P(A)$ a summand of that translated projective-injective, hence injective; projectivity of $P(A)$ is by definition. A projective-injective indecomposable is self-dual: $DP(A)=P(B)$ with $[P(A)]=[P(B)]$ because simple classes are duality-fixed and the Cartan matrix is $DD^{t}$ with unitriangular invertible $D$, so $A=B$. A self-dual $P(A)$ has its head in its socle, and its standard flag embeds that simple into a standard section; conversely if $A$ is standard then $P(A)$ is projective-injective by the previous sentence. BGG reciprocity and [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] identify the standard coefficients of $[P(A)]$ with the transpose composition matrix defining the quasi-canonical vector $P_A$ at $s=1$. Thus the normalization $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ of [F4] identifies that actual projective class with the source canonical vector at $s=1$, whose unitriangular monomial expansion has unique maximal label $A^{\uparrow}$. Since $P(A)$ is an indecomposable tilting object its unique maximal standard label identifies it as $T(A^{\uparrow})$.

**Conclusion.** Every label has a unique normalized indecomposable tilting object with the stated maximal-support flag, every tilting is a finite sum of these, restricted duality fixes them, lower ideals stabilize the same objects, and $P(A)$ is projective-injective exactly for standard $A$, in which case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$; no Irving criterion or future Schur-theoretic input is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small abelian category in which every object
has finite length. Let $\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)$ be the set of
isomorphism classes of simple objects. The homomorphism

$$\Phi:\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Simp}(\mathcal C)]\longrightarrow G_0(\mathcal C),\qquad e_{[S]}\longmapsto[S],$$

is an isomorphism. For any object $M$ and simple object $S$, the coordinate of
$[M]$ under $\Phi^{-1}$ at $e_{[S]}$ is $[M:S]$, the number of composition
factors isomorphic to $S$ in a composition series of $M$.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an essentially small additive category
([[def-additive-category]]), and let $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)$ be its set
of isomorphism classes. Its **split Grothendieck group** is

$$ K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathcal D):=\mathbb Z[\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)]\big/\langle e_{X\oplus Y}-e_X-e_Y\rangle, $$

where the free abelian group is generated by $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)$
([[def-free-abelian-group]]) and the subgroup is generated by the displayed
elements for all pairs $X,Y\in\mathcal D$. Write $[X]$ for the image of
$e_X$; then $[X\oplus Y]=[X]+[Y]$, including $[0]=0$. Only direct-sum
relations are imposed; the isomorphism class of a biproduct is independent of
its choice. In particular, for a finite-dimensional algebra $A$,
write $K_0(A)$ for this group on the additive category of finite-dimensional
projective left $A$-modules; it is distinct from the short-exact-sequence group
of all finite-dimensional $A$-modules.

An object $P$ of an abelian category is **projective** when for every epimorphism
$q:E\twoheadrightarrow M$ and every morphism $f:P\to M$, there exists a
morphism $\widetilde f:P\to E$ with

$$q\widetilde f=f.$$

The lift $\widetilde f$ need not be unique.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every projective object
of $\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

More precisely, each projective cover $P(\mu)$ produced by
[[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]] is a direct summand of the
projective object $\operatorname{pr}_C(E\otimes M(\lambda))$ of
[[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]], which is a
direct summand of $E\otimes M(\lambda)$; a general projective object has
finite length, hence is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives,
each of which is a projective cover of its simple head.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category in which every object has finite
length, and define an object to be **indecomposable** when it is nonzero and
every decomposition $X\cong Y\oplus Z$ has $Y=0$ or $Z=0$. Then:

1. every object of $\mathcal A$ is a finite direct sum of indecomposable
   objects;
2. the endomorphism ring of an indecomposable object is local, and for an
   endomorphism $f$ of an indecomposable object either $f$ is an isomorphism
   or $f$ is nilpotent;
3. the decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and permutation of the
   summands;
4. an indecomposable projective object $P$ of $\mathcal A$ has a unique
   maximal proper subobject $J(P)$, its quotient $P/J(P)$ is simple, and $P$
   is a projective cover of $P/J(P)$
   ([[def-projective-object]], [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]];
   projectivity here is relative to $\mathcal A$. In a full subcategory closed
   under submodules, essentiality is the superfluous-kernel condition of the
   cited module definition; projectivity in the ambient module category is
   not asserted).

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Ext-self-orthogonality and finite projective dimension.** Each $T(A)$ has a standard flag and each $T(B)$ has a costandard flag. All positive $\operatorname{Ext}$ groups between these two kinds of flags vanish by the locally proved criterion of [F1], giving $\operatorname{Ext}^i(T(A),T(B))=0$ for every $i>0$. The actual projective sequence onto each standard has a standard-filtered kernel with strictly higher labels; starting at maximal labels, where the standard is projective, downward induction on the finite poset gives finite projective dimension for every standard. Long exact sequences along a finite standard flag then give finite projective dimension for every $T(A)$ and their finite sum $T_\Gamma$. The second flag in the Ext argument is costandard, and no standard/standard Ext vanishing is assumed.

**Costandard presentations by tiltings.** Dual to the normalized standard inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)$, every costandard object admits a surjection from a tilting object with costandard-filtered kernel; induction on the costandard flag length gives such presentations for every costandard-filtered object.

**Exactness and full faithfulness of $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$.** On costandard flags the functor sends the presentations of step 2.1 to projective presentations of the images; two tilting presentations lift every map and identify its kernel, so the functor is exact on costandard-filtered objects and fully faithful. It sends tilting objects to projective objects because $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))$ is a direct summand of the regular module.

**The highest-weight structure of the dual.** The quotient $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))\to\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$ has a kernel filtered by standards with labels strictly higher in the reversed order, and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$ with head labelled $A$; this follows from full faithfulness in step 3.1 and the maximal tilting support of [F1]. Hence the Ringel-dual category is highest weight with the reversed poset and the displayed standards, and its filtered image is $\mathcal F(\Delta_R)$, not $\mathcal F(\nabla_R)$.

**Conclusion.** $T_\Gamma$ is a characteristic tilting generator with Ext-self-orthogonal summands and finite projective dimension, the Ringel-dual category has the reversed poset with standards $\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is an exact fully faithful equivalence from costandard-filtered objects to standard-filtered dual objects, exchanging tiltings with projectives; the algebraic realization is proved in the next theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
